1.meaning: Two of the 'disconnected letters' (al-muqaṭṭaʿāt) — the Arabic letters Ḥā and Mīm recited individually by name rather than read as a word. Several sūrahs open with such isolated letters; their precise meaning is known to Allah, and they serve to call attention and to point to the miraculous nature of a revelation composed from the very letters people use in their own speech.
1.grammar: These are letter-names recited individually, not an inflected word, so they carry no case ending or tense. The long pronunciation (ḥā, mīm) is how the letters are spelled out by name; they stand outside the normal grammar of a sentence.

1.meaning: A sending-down; the act of causing something to descend in stages from a higher source to a lower one. As a noun it commonly denotes something 'sent down' from on high, emphasizing the gradual, deliberate process of its descent.
1.grammar: A verbal noun of Form II (the doubled, intensive pattern), which conveys sending down bit by bit or repeatedly. The final '-un' (nunation) is the indefinite nominative ending: it marks the word as indefinite ('a sending-down') and in the subject/naming case, the form used when a noun stands as subject or as the predicate identifying something.
1.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, be sent down

2.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
2.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

3.meaning: The Most Merciful, the All-Compassionate — a name of Allah on an intensive pattern stressing immense, all-embracing mercy that encompasses the whole of creation. It denotes overflowing, universal compassion rather than an occasional act of kindness.
3.grammar: The al- prefix is the definite article 'the'; its 'l' assimilates in pronunciation into the following 'r' (heard as ar-raḥmān). The word is an intensive form on the faʿlān pattern, conveying fullness and vastness of the quality. The final -i is the genitive ending, used when a word follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun ('… OF …').

4.meaning: The Especially Merciful: one who actively and continually bestows mercy. From the divine attributes, it stresses mercy as ongoing, effective compassion shown to its recipients. The pattern (faʿīl) is intensive, conveying that this mercy is deep, constant, and abundant.
4.grammar: A definite adjective/name on the intensive faʿīl pattern. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun (as a description) or follows a preposition or oath particle.

1.meaning: A book, scripture, or written record — that which is written. It denotes a written document, and in the religious sense a revealed Scripture sent down from Allah.
1.grammar: A noun ('a book') with the -un ending, the nominative indefinite case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence. The form names a written or revealed text without specifying which.

2.meaning: To be set out distinctly and in detail — separated into clear parts, expounded and made fully plain so nothing is left vague.
2.grammar: A past-tense passive verb in the intensive pattern (the doubled middle letter conveys thoroughness): the u-i internal vowelling shows the action was done to the subject without naming a doer — 'it was set out in detail'. The final -at ending marks a single feminine subject ('it').
2.root: ف-ص-ل (f-ṣ-l) — to separate, distinguish, set out distinctly

3.meaning: His signs, tokens, or verses — the marks and indicators that point to a truth, including the verses of revelation, all belonging to Him (Allah).
3.grammar: A feminine plural noun with the -u nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence. The suffix -hu means 'his/its', showing the signs belong to a single masculine possessor.
3.root: ا-ي-ي / ء-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token that points to something.

4.meaning: A recitation, a reading; a text meant to be recited aloud. As a common noun it denotes 'something recited,' and as a proper name it is the Qur'an, the recited Scripture.
4.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'recitation.' The ending -an is accusative with nunation (the -n marking it indefinite, 'a recitation'); the accusative is the case typically marking the object of a verb or a noun being specified.

5.meaning: An adjective meaning 'Arabic' — pertaining to the Arabs or to their language; that which is in clear, eloquent Arabic speech.
5.grammar: A relational adjective formed with the -iyy suffix ('belonging to / characterized by'). The final -an (tanwīn) is the indefinite accusative: it marks an indefinite descriptive word agreeing with an indefinite accusative noun it qualifies ('an Arabic …').

6.meaning: For a people, for a folk or community; a group of human beings considered together. Joined to the preposition 'li' ('for / to').
6.grammar: The preposition 'li' ('for / to') plus an indefinite singular noun ('a people'). The -in ending (nunation) marks indefiniteness; it is the genitive form, required because nouns governed by 'li' stand in the genitive.
6.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a people/community

7.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
7.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: One who carries glad tidings; a herald or announcer of good news, a bringer of joy and welcome promises.
1.grammar: An intensive/agent noun on the pattern faʿīl, naming someone characterized by giving good news. The final -an (accusative with nunation, the doubled 'n' sound) marks it as indefinite and typically signals an object of a verb or a state/role ('as a …'). The nunation shows it is indefinite ('a bringer of good news').
1.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; (also) human skin/mankind

2.meaning: One who warns; a herald who cautions of impending danger or consequence, urging heedfulness.
2.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and', joining this to what precedes. The stem is an intensive/agent noun on the faʿīl pattern, naming one who warns. The final -an (accusative with nunation) marks it indefinite and typically signals an object or a state/role ('as a …').
2.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution; a solemn vow/pledge

3.meaning: so he turned away; a verb for averting oneself, turning one's side or back to something and shunning or disregarding it.
3.grammar: The prefixed fa- means 'so / then', linking the verb to a preceding action as its result or sequel. The verb is past tense in the causative pattern (Form IV) and here means to turn aside or shun. The final -a is the default ending of the third-person masculine singular in the past tense (the unmarked base form), so the subject is understood as 'he turned away'.
3.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — to be broad/side-on; (Form IV) to turn away, avert oneself

4.meaning: Most of them / the greater part of them — the noun 'akthar' (the greater number, the majority), built on a comparative/superlative pattern of k-th-r ('much/many'), with the pronoun 'them'.
4.grammar: A noun in possessive (genitive) construction: 'aktharu' ('the most of') plus the attached pronoun '-hum' ('them') yields 'most of them'. The '-u' on 'akthar' is the nominative ending, typical when this phrase serves as the subject.
4.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, numerous

5.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
5.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

6.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

7.meaning: They hear / listen to — to perceive by hearing, and often to give heed to what is heard.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the third-person masculine plural ('they'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual action.

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: Hearts — the seat of understanding, feeling, intention, and faith in a person. In Qur'anic usage the heart is the organ of comprehension and moral life, not merely the source of emotion.
2.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with the -u nominative ending, marking it as a subject. The attached -nā means 'our,' showing the hearts belong to the speakers.
2.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over; the heart

3.meaning: The preposition 'in / within / during.' It places something inside a container, period, place, or matter.
3.grammar: A preposition. It governs the noun that follows, putting it in the genitive case and situating something inside it — in space, in time ('during'), or in a circumstance.

4.meaning: Coverings, sheaths, or wrappings that screen something off and seal it from access — the kind of casing that envelops a thing so nothing can reach into or out of it; used figuratively of veils placed over hearts or minds.
4.grammar: A plural noun (the broken plural of kinān, a cover/sheath). The final -in (tanwīn kasra) is indefinite and genitive: the word is unspecified ('some coverings') and is in the case used after prepositions or to link it to a preceding noun.
4.root: ك-ن-ن (k-n-n) — to cover, conceal, shelter, enclose

5.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
5.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

6.meaning: You call us / you summon us / you invite us. It conveys calling out to, inviting, or summoning a person, with the speakers ('us') as the ones being called by a group ('you').
6.grammar: A present/imperfect verb in the second-person masculine plural ('you all'), shown by the ta- prefix together with the -ū plural-subject marker. The full indicative plural suffix is -ūna, but its final nūn is elided when the object pronoun -nā is attached, leaving -ū- directly before it. The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us', so the whole means 'you (all) call us'.
6.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

7.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
7.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

8.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
8.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

9.meaning: Our ears — the organs of hearing, here belonging to a group of speakers ('us').
9.grammar: A plural noun (the plural of udhun, 'ear') with the attached possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The -i ending is genitive, the case that follows prepositions or marks possession; the suffix -nā assigns ownership to a first-person plural group.
9.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — ear, hearing, to give heed / permission

10.meaning: Heaviness or deafness in the ear — a weight or dullness that blocks hearing, so that words do not get through; a plug-like obstruction of the sense of hearing.
10.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) is indefinite and nominative: 'a heaviness/deafness,' in the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being asserted to exist.
10.root: و-ق-ر (w-q-r) — heaviness, weight, gravity; dullness of hearing

11.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
11.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

12.meaning: 'Between us' / 'among us' — the space, relation, or midst that lies between parties; here bound to 'us'.
12.grammar: An adverbial noun of place meaning 'between/among'. The -i ending is genitive, here because the word takes a following pronoun in a possessive-style construction: it is bound to -nā ('us'), giving 'between us'. The suffix -nā is the attached first-person plural pronoun.
12.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, what lies between, distinctness

13.meaning: And between you — the preposition 'between' joined to 'you'. It marks the space or relation separating two sides, here naming one of those sides as 'you'.
13.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') plus the word 'between', which functions like a preposition of place. The -i ending is genitive, the case a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a following word ('... of ...'); on 'between' it sets up the pairing it governs. The attached -ka is 'you' (one male), naming one of the two parties.
13.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

14.meaning: A barrier, veil, or partition: something that screens off and separates one side from another, blocking sight or passage between them.
14.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation (the final -n), which marks the noun as indefinite — 'a barrier' rather than 'the barrier'.
14.root: ح-ج-ب (ḥ-j-b) — to screen, veil, block from view

15.meaning: So act / so work / so do — a command to put effort into action and carry out a deed, with an opening 'so/then' that draws a consequence from what came before.
15.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so/then,' linking a result to a preceding statement. The stem is a command (imperative) addressed to one male person. The bare, vowel-less ending (sukūn on the final letter) is the standard jussive form that marks a direct order to do something.
15.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to work, act, do, perform a deed

16.meaning: 'Indeed we …' — an emphatic opener that combines a particle of strong affirmation ('truly, certainly') with the pronoun 'we', stressing and confirming the statement that follows about the speakers.
16.grammar: The emphatic particle 'inna' ('indeed, truly') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('we'). 'Inna' introduces a sentence and lends it certainty and emphasis, while '-nā' is its subject, identifying the speakers as 'we'. This is the fuller, uncontracted form (innanā) of the commonly contracted innā; the extra nūn belongs to the longer pronominal base used to keep the doubled nūn of 'inna' and the nūn of the pronoun distinct rather than merged.

17.meaning: Ones who work, act, or do — people engaged in deeds and activity; those who carry out and perform.
17.grammar: An active participle ('working ones, doers') in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending is the masculine plural in the subject (nominative) case, the form used when the word is the doer or subject ('they are workers / they are acting').

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
2.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

3.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
3.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

4.meaning: 'A human being, a mortal man' — bashar denotes humankind as flesh-and-blood mortals. It emphasizes the human, bodily nature of a person.
4.grammar: A noun (also usable collectively for 'mankind'). The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a human being'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence (e.g. the one who acts) or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied.

5.meaning: One like you, your equal, of the same kind as you (addressing a group) — 'a like' or 'counterpart' joined to the plural 'you'. It asserts sameness of nature.
5.grammar: The noun mithl ('like, equal') with the attached pronoun -kum ('you', addressing a group of males or a mixed group). The -u ending is nominative, typically marking the word as the subject or as a predicate ('… is one like you').
5.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, resemblance; a match or equal

6.meaning: 'It is revealed / inspired' — for a message to be conveyed by Allah to a prophet, whether by inspiration, sign, or revealed word. This is the passive sense: the revelation is sent to the recipient.

parts.en: he/it (third-person masculine present prefix, passive vowel)
is revealed / inspired (passive stem ending in a long final vowel)

6.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice: the 'yu-' prefix with the internal vowel pattern means 'it is (being) revealed' — the action is done TO the subject. The verb ends in a fixed long '-ā' vowel because its final root letter is weak; this form is the same in the passive present regardless of case.
6.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — revelation, inspiration, conveying a message

7.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
7.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

8.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that …' or 'only that' — it introduces and emphasizes a fact as the content of a thought or statement; 'anna' asserts ('indeed/that') and the attached 'mā' often gives a restrictive sense ('that … is only …').
8.grammar: A combination of the emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with 'mā'. 'Anna' introduces a noun-clause as the object of verbs like 'think' or 'know', putting the following noun in the accusative. Joined with 'mā' it frequently carries a limiting force, 'only/merely'. Particles like this do not themselves take case endings.

9.meaning: Your god/deity (addressing a group) — the one deemed worthy of worship, the object of devotion. Ilāh denotes 'a god, an object of worship'; with -kum it means 'your god'.
9.grammar: The noun ilāh ('god, deity') with the attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your', addressing a group). The -u ending is nominative, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate ('your god is …').
9.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, divinity; being worshipped and turned to in devotion

10.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
10.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
10.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

11.meaning: One / single and unique — denoting oneness: a single individual, undivided and without partner or plurality.
11.grammar: An adjective/numeral meaning 'one.' The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typically used for a subject, predicate, or a descriptor agreeing with such a noun.
11.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — oneness, singularity, uniqueness

12.meaning: 'So stand firm / be upright / keep straight' — a command to a group of males to be steadfast, hold a straight and correct course, and remain firmly committed. The leading 'fa-' means 'then / so', linking the order to what came before.
12.grammar: A command (imperative) in the Form X (is-ta-…) pattern, addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group), meaning 'make yourselves upright / hold a straight course'. The ending -ū marks the plural addressees 'you all'. The prefixed fa- means 'then' or 'so', connecting the command to a preceding clause.
12.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

13.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
13.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

14.meaning: And seek forgiveness from Him — a call to ask Allah to cover over and pardon one's sins, directed at a group, with the object 'Him' attached.
14.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The stem is a Form X imperative — the pattern istaf'ala that means 'to seek/ask for' the action — so it means 'ask for forgiveness.' The plural-command ending -ū addresses several people ('all of you, do this'); the attached -hu ('Him') is the one being asked.
14.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to forgive, pardon, cover over (sins)

15.meaning: And woe — an exclamation announcing impending doom, ruin, or grievous punishment upon someone; a cry of warning and lament rather than a simple noun.
15.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'wayl' is a noun of doom used in exclamations. The '-un' ending (nunation) is indefinite nominative; with such exclamatory nouns it commonly introduces the one threatened with 'woe to…'.

16.meaning: For / belonging to the polytheists — those who associate partners with Allah, ascribing divinity or worship to others alongside Him.
16.grammar: Built from the preposition li- ('for/to') + the definite article al- ('the') + an active participle ('those who associate partners with Allah'). The masculine sound-plural ending -īna (here the preposition shortens its written form) is the oblique case used after prepositions and for possession, marking a plural group of people.
16.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, make a partner

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: A plural present verb: 'they give, they bestow, they hand over.' It denotes the act of granting or delivering something to others.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb of the form-IV pattern ('to give'). The yu-…-ūna framing marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the final -na is the indicative ending, marking an ordinary, ongoing statement.
3.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to give, to bring

4.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
4.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
4.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

5.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
5.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.

6.meaning: "in / with the Hereafter" — the preposition "in/with" joined to the noun for the next world, the final, lasting abode that comes after this present life.
6.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition ("in, with, by") and the al- means "the." Because of the preposition, the noun takes the genitive -i ending. The word itself is built on the adjective "latter/last," used as a name for the world to come.
6.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after

7.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
7.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

8.meaning: Disbelievers / deniers: those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The active participle names people characterized by ungrateful rejection of what should be acknowledged.
8.grammar: A masculine plural active participle. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or predicate (as opposed to -īna for object/genitive).
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
6.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

7.meaning: Means 'a reward, a wage, a recompense'. The word denotes the due return for work or deeds — payment earned, compensation, or a reward.
7.grammar: A noun in the nominative, indefinite ('a reward'). The -un ending (a doubled-vowel tanwīn) marks both indefiniteness ('a/some') and the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a thing being asserted to exist ('there is a reward').

8.meaning: 'Other than, except, not' — a word of exception or difference that sets one thing apart from another, or negates an attribute ('non-…').
8.grammar: A noun of exclusion meaning 'other than.' It governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than ___ '). The '-u' nominative ending typically reflects its agreement with, or role describing, a preceding nominative noun.

9.meaning: Cut off / unceasing — the word mamnūn here carries the sense of something that is not cut off, unending, without cessation. The context (surah 68:3) speaks of an unceasing reward for the Prophet.
9.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) from the root م-ن-ن (m-n-n), which carries meanings of both bestowal and cutting off. Here with the preceding negation (ghayr) it means 'not cut off' = unceasing. Indefinite, genitive case (-in tanwīn).

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A charged question-opener meaning roughly 'Is it really the case that you (plural)…?' — a questioning particle fused with an emphasis particle (inna, 'indeed/truly') and 'you'. It poses a question while underscoring the claim being questioned, often with a tone of astonishment or challenge.
2.grammar: An interrogative prefix a- ('do/is it that…?') joined to the emphasizing particle inna ('indeed'). Inna places the noun or pronoun following it (its ism) in the accusative; here that is the attached -kum ('you', plural), which functions logically like the subject of the statement but stands formally in the accusative. The combination both asks and stresses, and the -kum addresses a group.
2.root: — (particles; no root)

3.meaning: You surely disbelieve / reject — to deny and turn away in ungrateful rejection of the truth, emphatically affirmed of a group ('you really do disbelieve').
3.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphasis marker ('truly/surely'). The ta-…-ūna frame is a present/ongoing verb addressed to 'you (plural)': the ta- prefix signals the addressee and the -ūna ending marks a plural subject doing the action now or habitually.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to disbelieve, deny, be ungrateful, cover up (truth)

4.meaning: A combination meaning 'with/for the one that' or 'in exchange for that which'. It fuses the preposition bi- (with, by, in exchange for) onto the masculine singular relative pronoun alladhī ('the one who/that'), introducing a clause that further identifies the referred-to thing.

parts.en: the one who/that (masc. sing. relative pronoun)

4.grammar: bi- is a preposition that always governs a genitive; alladhī is an indeclinable masculine singular relative pronoun whose form does not change for case. It points to a single masculine entity and requires a following clause to complete its sense ('the one that …').

5.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
5.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

6.meaning: 'the earth,' 'the ground,' 'the land' — the earth as a whole, or the land/ground beneath us. It denotes the terrestrial expanse on which creatures live and walk.
6.grammar: A definite noun ('the earth'). The '-a' ending marks the accusative (the 'object' case) — the role of the thing acted upon, e.g. the direct object of a verb. The prefixed 'al-' makes it definite, 'the earth.'
6.root: أ-ر-ض (ʼ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: 'Two days' — the dual form referring to exactly two days.
8.grammar: A dual noun (denoting exactly two). The ending -ayni is the dual marker in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition, or as a direct object, or as the second part of a possessive pair.

9.meaning: And you (a group) make, render, set, or appoint something to be a certain way, or place it in a certain status — to turn one thing into another or assign it a role.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'wa-' is the connector 'and'. The stem 'tajʿal' on its own carries the 2nd-person singular ('you [one] make'); plurality is supplied only by the added '-ūna', so the 't-' prefix together with that ending yields 'you all' (second person masculine plural) acting now or habitually. This 'jaʿala' commonly takes two objects ('to make X [into] Y'). The '-ūna' (rather than '-ū') shows the verb is in its plain, unaltered present state.
9.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, place, appoint, assign

10.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
10.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

11.meaning: The plural of 'nidd': 'rivals', 'equals', or 'peers' — things set up as comparable or equal to something else, especially false objects of worship set up alongside Allah.
11.grammar: 'andād' is a broken (irregular) plural of 'nidd'. The '-an' ending (tanwīn al-fatḥ) marks an indefinite noun in the accusative case, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb ('… some rivals').
11.root: ن-د-د (n-d-d) — to be equal/rival, a counterpart or match

12.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
12.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

13.meaning: The Lord of — owner, master and sustainer who creates, possesses and governs. Of Allah it names the One who brings up and maintains all that exists.
13.grammar: The noun 'rabb' with the final -u marking the nominative case (subject or predicate: '… is the Lord'). Standing before a following noun it carries the sense 'Lord of …'. It combines ownership, authority and nurturing care.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing

14.meaning: The worlds, all created realms — the totality of beings and peoples; in 'Lord of the worlds,' the whole of creation across all its kinds.
14.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the worlds') with 'al-' ('the'). The '-īna' ending marks a masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) form — the form used after a preposition, in an 'of' linkage, or as a direct object.
14.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know; a 'world' as a sign by which the Creator is known

1.meaning: 'And he made / appointed / rendered' — the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to make something into something, to fashion or appoint it. It can mean to create, to assign, or to cause a thing to become a certain way.
1.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare verb with its final -a vowel denotes a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he made/did').
1.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

2.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
2.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
2.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

3.meaning: Firmly anchored, towering mountains — heights that stand immovable and steady, often pictured as stabilising the earth.
3.grammar: A plural noun in the 'broken plural' pattern, denoting mountains as firmly fixed. The final -a here is the accusative ending typical of this diptote pattern (which resists the usual -in), marking the word as an object or in a similar role.
3.root: ر-س-و (r-s-w) — to be firm, anchored, immovably fixed

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: Above them — fawqihā means 'above them', where fawqa (above) and -hā (them/it, referring to the chambers or their levels) describe the multi-tiered nature of the mansions.

parts.en: them, it (third person feminine pronoun — referring to the chambers)

5.grammar: Fawq is a noun used prepositionally meaning 'above', in the genitive after the implied preposition. The suffix -hā refers back to ghurafun (chambers) treated as a non-rational plural (feminine). The verse describes chambers built upon chambers — lofty multi-storied mansions.

6.meaning: And He blessed / placed lasting good and abundance in — to imbue something with enduring divine goodness, growth, and benefit that keeps increasing.
6.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The stem is a Form III past-tense verb (the ā-pattern fā'ala) meaning 'to bless.' The final -a marks a completed past action done by a single male subject ('He blessed').
6.root: ب-ر-ك (b-r-k) — blessing, abundance, lasting goodness

7.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
7.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

8.meaning: 'and he plotted' or 'and he calculated (maliciously)' — a third-person masculine singular perfect verb expressing careful, devious planning or measurement. Describes the wrongdoer's scheming against the Prophet's message.

parts.en: he plotted / he calculated / he measured (perfect Form II)

8.grammar: Wāw is a connective conjunction. Qaddara is the third-person masculine singular perfect active of the Form II verb qaddara (to calculate, to estimate, to plot), root q-d-r. Form II doubles the dāl.

9.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
9.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

10.meaning: Its foodstuffs / sustenance / provisions — the nourishment and means of subsistence that belong to it.
10.grammar: A plural noun (the plural of qūt, 'nourishment/sustenance') with the attached possessive -hā ('its/her'). The -a ending is accusative, the case that commonly marks the direct object of a verb; the suffix -hā assigns ownership to a single feminine/non-human thing.
10.root: ق-و-ت (q-w-t) — nourishment, food, sustenance

11.meaning: The preposition 'in / within / during.' It places something inside a container, period, place, or matter.
11.grammar: A preposition. It governs the noun that follows, putting it in the genitive case and situating something inside it — in space, in time ('during'), or in a circumstance.

12.meaning: 'Four' — the cardinal number four.
12.grammar: A cardinal number with the feminine -at ending (used when counting masculine nouns). The -i case ending is genitive, the form taken after a preposition or when linked to a following counted noun ('… of …').
12.root: ر-ب-ع (r-b-ʿ) — four, a fourth

13.meaning: Days — the plural of 'day,' periods of daylight or twenty-four-hour spans.
13.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of yawm ('day'). The ending -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('days') and in the genitive case, the form used in a possessive link ('… of days') or after a preposition.
13.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time

14.meaning: 'Equal / the same / alike' — a noun-adjective expressing equality or sameness; that two or more things stand on a par, with no difference between them. It can also mean a level or even thing.
14.grammar: A noun/adjective. The ending -an is accusative with nunation: the -n sound marks it as indefinite, and the accusative case commonly marks it as a predicate or the thing described/acted upon. The accusative -an is here written with a supporting alif (ـاء).
14.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — being level, equal, even, in balance

15.meaning: 'for those who ask / for the questioners' — refers to people who request, inquire, or seek something, marked as the beneficiaries by an attached 'for/to'.
15.grammar: An active participle ('one who asks') made definite by 'the' and put in the sound masculine plural. The plural ending -īna is the form used for the object of a preposition or a direct object (the oblique/accusative form), as opposed to -ūna which marks the subject. The prefix li- means 'for' or 'to' and pulls the noun into this oblique form. The doubled 'l' of li- assimilates into the article.

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: 'He turned (His attention) to', 'He settled upon', or 'He became evenly established' — a verb of rising to / directing oneself toward something and setting it in balanced order; depending on context it can mean to mount, to settle over, or to become level and complete.
2.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'). It is a form X verb (the istaf'ala pattern, marked by the sīn-tā' prefix placed before the root, often adding a reflexive or 'seeking/becoming' sense). The final long -ā is how the past-tense 'he' ending appears on verbs whose last root letter is a weak vowel; the initial i- is a helping vowel needed to begin the word.
2.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — evenness, levelling, being balanced/complete

3.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
3.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

4.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
4.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

5.meaning: and it / and she — the conjunction 'and' joined to a standalone subject pronoun meaning 'it' or 'she', pointing to something feminine in gender.
5.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and'. The word hiya is an independent subject pronoun for a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) entity, 'it/she'. As a standalone pronoun it typically begins a descriptive statement about that thing.

6.meaning: Smoke — the visible vapor or fume that rises from burning; also used of a haze or pall.
6.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamma) is indefinite and nominative: 'smoke / a smoke,' in the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a thing being identified.
6.root: د-خ-ن (d-kh-n) — smoke, fume, haze

7.meaning: 'Then he said / so he said' — the past-tense verb 'he said,' introduced by a connector meaning 'then / so,' marking what follows as the next or resulting step.
7.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then / so,' linking this to what came before and often implying sequence or consequence. The verb is past-tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final -a is the base vowel of the 3rd-person masculine singular past form, marking that a single masculine subject performed the action.

8.meaning: 'For it / to it, belonging to it' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to a pronoun referring to a feminine singular thing; it expresses possession or benefit ('it has / it gets').
8.grammar: Preposition 'li-' (here vowelled 'la-' before a pronoun) plus an attached object pronoun. The -hā suffix means 'it/her,' a feminine singular. Pronouns that follow a preposition are in the genitive (object-of-preposition) role; -hā is a fixed form and does not change shape.

9.meaning: And to / for the earth — the ground, the land, the world below the sky, marked as the one being addressed or the one to whom something belongs.
9.grammar: Built from wa- ('and') + the preposition li- ('to/for') + the article al- ('the') + the noun 'earth.' The final -i is genitive, the case required after a preposition, here marking the earth as the thing addressed or the recipient of an action.

10.meaning: Come, you two! — a command to two parties to come or to present themselves / arrive.
10.grammar: An imperative (command) built on the root for 'coming.' The ending -ā is the dual marker: it directs the order to exactly two addressees ('the two of you, come').
10.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring

11.meaning: 'Willingly, obediently, of one's own accord' — acting out of voluntary compliance and submission rather than compulsion.
11.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The -an ending (with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) is the accusative, here describing the manner of an action — 'willingly, in a state of compliance.'
11.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — obedience, willing compliance

12.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
12.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

13.meaning: A noun used adverbially meaning 'by force, against one's will, under compulsion / with reluctance,' i.e., something done unwillingly or imposed.
13.grammar: A verbal noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative; on a noun like this it functions adverbially, describing the manner or circumstance of an action ('forcibly,' 'reluctantly').
13.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — disliking, aversion, compulsion

14.meaning: They two said / they both said — a completed act of speaking by two parties.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb ('said'). The ending -tā combines the feminine marker with the dual: it marks a completed action done by exactly two feminine/non-human subjects ('the two of them said').

15.meaning: We came / We brought — the first-person plural of coming, also used in the sense of bringing or producing something.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached -nā marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The verb's core sense is 'to come'; with an object it carries the sense 'to bring / to bring forth'.

16.meaning: Willingly, obediently, of one's own accord — being compliant and yielding, doing something gladly rather than under compulsion; said of a group.
16.grammar: An active participle ('one who willingly obeys') in the masculine sound plural. The ending -īna is the oblique/accusative form of that plural, used here to describe the state or manner of a group ('coming willingly') — the case for objects and circumstantial descriptions.
16.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply, do willingly

1.meaning: Then He decreed / completed / brought them to their finished state — to settle a matter conclusively and carry it through to completion, with 'them' as the object.
1.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then/so.' The stem is a past-tense verb meaning to decree, finish, or settle conclusively; its final long -ā marks a completed action by a single male subject ('He'). The attached -hunna is the object pronoun 'them,' referring to a feminine plural group.
1.root: ق-ض-ي (q-ḍ-y) — to decree, settle, complete, judge

2.meaning: 'Seven' — the cardinal number seven.
2.grammar: A cardinal number. The final -a is the accusative case ending, the form a noun typically takes when it is the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon) or otherwise governed into that case. The counted noun following it normally appears in the genitive ('of') form.
2.root: س-ب-ع (s-b-ʿ) — the number seven

3.meaning: Heavens / skies — the celestial expanses above; the plural of 'heaven,' indicating the layered skies.
3.grammar: A feminine sound-plural noun ('heavens'). The ending -in (tanwīn kasra) is indefinite and, for this plural type, marks both the genitive and accusative cases — used after prepositions, to show possession, or as an object; here it signals an unspecified count of heavens.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: 'Two days' — the dual form referring to exactly two days.
5.grammar: A dual noun (denoting exactly two). The ending -ayni is the dual marker in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition, or as a direct object, or as the second part of a possessive pair.

6.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and He inspired / revealed / instilled' — awḥā is to convey something swiftly and privately: to put into the heart, to direct by inspiration, or to send revelation.
6.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') with a Form IV past-tense verb. The bare third-person masculine singular form ('he/it did') ends in a final long -ā (a weak-final verb). It denotes a completed action of inspiring, instilling, or revealing.
6.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — to inspire, suggest, reveal swiftly

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

8.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
8.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

9.meaning: A heaven / a sky — one of the celestial expanses above the earth.
9.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) is indefinite and genitive: 'a heaven,' in the case used after prepositions or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… of a heaven').

10.meaning: Its matter / affair / command / ordained business — the concern, charge, or directive belonging to it; what it is appointed to do.
10.grammar: A singular noun (amr means both 'command' and 'affair/matter') with the attached possessive -hā ('its'). The -a ending is accusative, the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb; the suffix -hā assigns ownership to a single feminine/non-human thing.
10.root: أ-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, order; matter, affair

11.meaning: And We adorned / beautified / decorated — to make something beautiful and attractive by furnishing it with ornament, done by 'We.'
11.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The stem is a Form II past-tense verb (the doubled-middle pattern fa''ala, which intensifies: to thoroughly beautify/decorate). The suffix -nā marks a completed past action done by a first-person plural subject ('We adorned'); its initial nūn merges with the stem's final nūn, producing the doubled spelling.
11.root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n) — adornment, beauty, decoration

12.meaning: The sky or heaven — all that rises and spreads overhead: the visible canopy above and the heights beyond it. A definite noun with the article 'al-', so 'the sky / the heaven'.
12.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', here assimilated to 'as-samāʾ'). The final '-a' ending is accusative: it typically marks the word as the object of a verb — the thing an action is done to — or the item being mentioned after certain particles.
12.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — to be high, lofty; that which is elevated overhead

13.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
13.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
13.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

14.meaning: With lamps — light-giving vessels, illuminations. The base noun maṣābīḥ is the plural of miṣbāḥ, a lamp or light, here governed by the preposition 'with/by'.
14.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of'. The noun is a 'broken' (irregular) plural on the mafāʿīl pattern. Such plurals are 'diptotes' — they take a single -a for the genitive instead of the usual -i, and they reject the indefinite doubled ending. So the final -a here is the genitive (required after the preposition), shown by 'a' rather than 'i'.

15.meaning: And as a guarding / and for protection — the word expresses the act of guarding and protecting from something.
15.grammar: Wa- is the conjunction 'and'. Ḥifẓan is a verbal noun (maṣdar) from ḥ-f-ẓ (to guard, preserve, protect). The -an ending (accusative indefinite tanwīn) makes it an adverbial accusative of purpose or a coordinate object.
15.root: ح-ف-ظ (ḥ-f-ẓ) — to guard, protect, preserve, memorise

16.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
16.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

17.meaning: A measuring out, determination, or precise ordaining — the act of setting things in exact proportion and decree. It denotes deliberately apportioning and fixing the measure of something.
17.grammar: A verbal noun of the causative pattern. The final '-u' is the nominative case, typically marking the word as a subject or predicate ('it is the ordaining…'). In a possessive construction it links to a following noun ('the ordaining OF …').

18.meaning: One who is mighty, invincible, and unassailable — possessing overwhelming might and dignity that none can overcome; also carries the sense of being precious and held in high honor. As a divine name it points to Allah's irresistible power.
18.grammar: A definite adjective/noun on the intensive paradigm faʿīl, denoting a deeply established quality. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the Mighty') or follows a preposition.

19.meaning: The All-Knowing — one whose knowledge is complete, encompassing all things, the hidden and the open. As an intensive form it denotes perfect, exhaustive knowing, not merely 'one who knows'.
19.grammar: A definite intensive adjective (the 'fully/utterly knowing one') with the article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' is the genitive case: it typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the All-Knowing'), often as a describing word agreeing with a genitive noun.

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

2.meaning: they turn away / they move away. Refers to the dignified act of distancing oneself from something unworthy — walking away rather than engaging.

parts.en: they turned away, they moved away (Form IV, past 3rd plural)

2.grammar: Past-tense verb (māḍī), 3rd person masculine plural, Form IV (aʿraḍa — to turn away, to disregard). The -ū ending marks the plural.
2.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — breadth; Form IV: to turn away, to show one's broadside (i.e., to ignore)

3.meaning: Then say! / so say!: a command to one person to speak or utter, joined to what precedes by 'then/so'.
3.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male, 'say!' The prefixed 'fa-' means 'then' or 'so', linking the command to something before it as a consequence or sequel. The bare, vowel-less ending is normal for this imperative.

4.meaning: I have warned you / given you cautioning notice — to alert someone to impending danger so they may guard against it; a first-person speaker addressing a group.
4.grammar: A Form IV past-tense verb (the af'ala pattern, which makes it causative: 'to make aware of danger / to warn'). The suffix -tu marks the doer as 'I' in a completed past action; the attached -kum is the object 'you,' addressed to a plural group.
4.root: ن-ذ-ر (n-dh-r) — to warn, caution, give notice of danger

5.meaning: A thunderbolt / a stunning blast — a sudden, overwhelming strike (a lightning-bolt or shattering cry) that fells or stuns whatever it hits.
5.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is indefinite and accusative: 'a thunderbolt,' in the case that commonly marks the direct object of a verb or the thing one is warned about.
5.root: ص-ع-ق (ṣ-ʿ-q) — thunderclap, stunning strike, to be struck senseless

6.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'like,' 'similar to,' 'the equal of,' or 'a counterpart.' It expresses likeness or correspondence between things.
6.grammar: A noun in the accusative ending -a. This ending typically marks it as the object of a verb, as an adverbial 'in like manner,' or as the first term of a possessive link ('the like of …'). It conveys resemblance or equivalence to whatever it is paired with.
6.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, comparison

7.meaning: A thunderbolt / stunning blast — a sudden, overpowering strike (lightning or a shattering cry) that fells or stuns; the same noun in a linking (genitive) form.
7.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -i is genitive, the case used after prepositions or to link the word to a preceding noun ('the … of a thunderbolt'); shown here without tanwīn, so it reads as definite or bound to a following word.
7.root: ص-ع-ق (ṣ-ʿ-q) — thunderclap, stunning strike, to be struck senseless

8.meaning: An active participle meaning 'one who transgresses, oversteps, goes beyond the limit'. It describes a person who exceeds proper bounds, acting in hostility or excess.
8.grammar: An active participle (doer pattern, originally ʿādiy → ʿādin), masculine singular, used as a noun/adjective. The -in ending is indefinite nunation in the genitive case — marking 'a transgressor' and the case used after prepositions or in noun-to-noun linkage.
8.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — to overstep, transgress, show enmity

9.meaning: And Thamūd — the name of an ancient Arabian people (the nation of the prophet Ṣāliḥ), known for carving homes in the rock and destroyed after rejecting their messenger.
9.grammar: A proper name (a people) with an -a ending and no 'tanwīn' (no final -n): it is 'diptote,' meaning it does not take the indefinite -n and uses -a for both the object and the after-preposition/linked positions. So this single -a form covers what would otherwise be two different case endings.

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

2.meaning: 'It / she came to them'. A past-tense verb of coming or arriving, with a feminine singular subject ('it/she'), and an attached pronoun 'them' as the ones reached.
2.grammar: 'jāa' is a past-tense verb 'came'. The '-t' suffix marks a feminine singular subject ('she' or a feminine 'it'). The attached '-hum' means 'them' (masculine plural) as the object reached; its vowel appears as '-humu' to ease pronunciation before a following word.
2.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, to arrive, to bring

3.meaning: "the messengers" — the definite plural of rasūl, an envoy or messenger: one sent with a message or mission. With the article it denotes 'the messengers' as a defined group.
3.grammar: A definite broken (internally formed) plural noun. The leading al- is 'the', and its 'l' assimilates into the following r- (heard as rr-). The final -u is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'between, in the midst of, the space separating two things.' It denotes the interval or position dividing one side from another, and is regularly used to express 'between X and Y.'
5.grammar: A noun of place that functions adverbially ('between / in the midst of'). The final -i ending is genitive, which typically links the word to a following noun ('… between … OF …') or marks it as governed by a preposition. Here the -i shows it is bound to whatever noun follows it.

6.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
6.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.
6.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand

7.meaning: 'And from / and out of / and among.' A connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'from,' which marks origin, source, a starting point, or 'some of' a larger whole.
7.grammar: Two particles: the connector 'wa-' ('and') and the preposition 'min.' 'Min' indicates origin or source ('from'), a starting point, or partition ('some of'). Particles do not change their endings.

8.meaning: Means 'behind them' or 'in their rear'. The base word denotes what is behind, the back, the rear, or those who come after; with the attached pronoun it becomes 'their behind / their rear / those left after them'.
8.grammar: A noun in the genitive case, shown by the -i ending on 'khalf-'. The genitive here arises because the noun follows a preposition or is the first term of a possessive pair. The attached pronoun -him means 'their' (referring to a masculine/mixed plural) and the form -him (rather than -hum) reflects that genitive context.
8.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to be behind, to come after, succession

9.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that … not,' 'lest,' 'so as not to.' It introduces a clause of something feared, intended-to-prevent, or negated after a verb.
9.grammar: A merging of the particle an ('that,' which introduces a verb in the subjunctive) with the negative lā ('not'); the 'n' of an assimilates into lā, giving allā. Together they mean 'that … not' and put the following verb into the subjunctive mood, often after verbs of fearing, wishing, or commanding.

10.meaning: (That) you should serve and worship — to direct devotion, obedience, and humble submission to one worthy of it; the act of ʻībāda (worship) addressed to a group.
10.grammar: A present/subjunctive verb. The ta- prefix marks a 'you' subject, and the -ū ending makes it plural ('you all'). When governed by a preceding particle the form takes the subjunctive ('that you may worship'); the dropped final nūn (written ū rather than ūna) reflects that subjunctive/jussive state.
10.root: ع-ب-د (ʻ-b-d) — to serve, worship, submit

11.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
11.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
12.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
12.root: — (proper name)

13.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
13.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

14.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
14.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

15.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
15.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

16.meaning: 'Our Lord' — 'Rabb' (Lord, Master, Sustainer who creates, owns, nurtures and governs) joined to 'our'. A weighty term for Allah as the One who brings up and sustains all that exists.
16.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive pronoun '-nā' ('our'). The -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, used when the word is the subject or predicate of a sentence ('[He] is our Lord').
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

17.meaning: He would surely have sent down / caused to descend — to bring something down from above (such as revelation or rain), emphatically affirmed as a definite outcome.
17.grammar: The prefix la- is an emphasis marker ('surely/certainly'), often answering an 'if' clause to assert its result. The stem is a Form IV past-tense verb (af'ala, causative: 'to make come down / send down'). The final -a marks a completed action done by a single male subject ('He sent down').
17.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to come down, descend; to send down

18.meaning: 'angels' — the plural of malak (angel), referring to the heavenly beings. Here describing the nineteen guards of Hell.
18.grammar: Feminine broken plural (jamʿ taksīr) of malak (angel), in the accusative (manṣūb) marked by tanwīn fatḥa. Malāʾika is the standard broken plural of malak, from the root m-l-k (or l-ʾ-k). Functions as the predicate complement.

19.meaning: Then indeed we: 'we' stated with emphasis and a connecting 'then/so'. The particle inna strongly affirms the statement, while the prefix fa- ties it as a consequence to what came before.
19.grammar: The connective fa- ('then, so', often marking a result) prefixed to the emphasizing particle inna ('indeed, truly'), with the attached first-person plural pronoun -nā meaning 'we/us' (the doubled nūn shared between inna and the pronoun is written once as a shadda). After inna a pronoun takes this object-style form. The whole emphatically asserts a statement about 'we' as a consequence.

20.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
20.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

21.meaning: 'You have been sent / were sent.' The verb is passive: it speaks of being dispatched or commissioned by someone else, as messengers are sent with a charge. The form addresses a group ('you all').
21.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice, built on the causative 'sending' form ('to be sent / dispatched'). The attached -tum ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), here the ones receiving the action. The past tense presents the sending as already accomplished.

22.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
22.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

23.meaning: Disbelievers / deniers: those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The active participle names people characterized by ungrateful rejection of what should be acknowledged.
23.grammar: A masculine plural active participle. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or predicate (as opposed to -īna for object/genitive).
23.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: 'Then as for …' A connective opening that introduces and singles out a topic for comment, often paired later with a response. The fa- means 'then/so,' and 'ammā' sets up 'as for (such-and-such)…' to highlight one case among others.
1.grammar: A connector fa- ('then, so') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā introduces a subject for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that gives the comment about it. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: The proper name 'ʿĀd' — an ancient Arabian people to whom a messenger was sent. As a name it denotes that nation/tribe.
2.grammar: A proper noun bearing the nominative case with nunation (-un), which generally marks it as the subject of a sentence. Being treated as fully declinable with tanwīn, it is often understood as the name of the tribe/people rather than a single individual.
2.root: — (proper name; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: So they grew proud / were arrogant — to swell with self-importance, to be haughty and refuse out of pride to submit or accept the truth.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the form X pattern (istakbara, 'to be arrogant'), 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The -ū ending shows a plural subject performing the completed action. The fa- prefix marks sequence or contrast ('so, but then').
3.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be great; (form X) to deem oneself great, be arrogant

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

6.meaning: 'Without' or 'other than' — the preposition bi- joined to ghayr, a noun meaning 'other than / not / lacking', together conveying the absence of something ('with no …', 'wrongfully').
6.grammar: bi- is a preposition that takes the genitive; ghayr is a noun of exception/negation ('other than'). Its -i ending is genitive (required after bi-) and it also links to a following noun in a possessive 'of' relationship, so 'bi-ghayri X' means 'without X / other than X'.
6.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, being other than

7.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
7.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
7.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

8.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
