8.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

9.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
9.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

10.meaning: 'Harder / more intense / stronger.' A comparative meaning something is greater in hardness, severity, force, or intensity than what it is compared with; the base sense is being firm, severe, and strong.
10.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('more severe / harder'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject or as the descriptive predicate of the subject. Built on the 'afʿal' pattern used for comparisons ('more …').
10.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be firm, intense, severe, strong

11.meaning: "from us" — the preposition 'from' (indicating origin, source, or starting point) fused with the attached pronoun 'us'. It can also carry a partitive sense, 'some of us / a part of us'.
11.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The base 'min' normally takes a vowelless final consonant, but before the pronoun '-nā' the nūn is doubled (assimilation), giving 'minnā'. The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural object/possessive pronoun meaning 'us' or 'our'.
11.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

12.meaning: Strength, power, force, might — physical or military vigour, robustness, and the capacity to exert force or prevail. Also used for firmness and resolve.
12.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the -an ending (the 'tanwīn' or 'n' of indefiniteness), so 'a strength / some power' with no 'the.' The accusative -an form is commonly used to specify in what respect something is meant ('in terms of strength') or as the object of a verb.
12.root: ق-و-ي (q-w-y) — to be strong; strength, power

13.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
13.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').
13.root: — (particles)

14.meaning: To see, perceive, or behold — and, by extension, to realize, observe, or come to recognize. The bare form here is the 'cut-short' (jussive) shape used after certain particles, so it reads 'they (do not) see'.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb in its shortened (jussive) form, used after particles such as those that negate the past or express purpose/condition. The third-person masculine plural subject 'they' here takes the distinct jussive plural ending '-aw' (written wāw + a silent 'alif al-fāriqa). This '-aw' is the jussive paradigm's own ending in its own right, not the indicative '-ūna' with the 'na' stripped off.

15.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
15.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
16.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

17.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
17.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

18.meaning: He created them — a verb expressing the act of bringing a group into existence from nothing, with 'them' as the ones created.
18.grammar: A past-tense verb ('he created') with an attached object pronoun. The bare verb with -a is third-person masculine singular ('he'); the suffix -hum is the object 'them' (masculine plural). So: 'he created them.'

19.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
19.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

20.meaning: 'Harder / more intense / stronger.' A comparative meaning something is greater in hardness, severity, force, or intensity than what it is compared with; the base sense is being firm, severe, and strong.
20.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('more severe / harder'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the word as the subject or as the descriptive predicate of the subject. Built on the 'afʿal' pattern used for comparisons ('more …').
20.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be firm, intense, severe, strong

21.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
21.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.

22.meaning: Strength, power, force, might — physical or military vigour, robustness, and the capacity to exert force or prevail. Also used for firmness and resolve.
22.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the -an ending (the 'tanwīn' or 'n' of indefiniteness), so 'a strength / some power' with no 'the.' The accusative -an form is commonly used to specify in what respect something is meant ('in terms of strength') or as the object of a verb.
22.root: ق-و-ي (q-w-y) — to be strong; strength, power

23.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
23.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

24.meaning: By/in Our signs. Āyāt is the plural of āya — a sign, token, or evidence. Signs are pointers that indicate a greater reality. With the prefixed particle and pronoun it means 'with/in Our signs'.
24.grammar: A plural noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, in, by'), which requires the following noun to take the -i (genitive) ending. The attached -nā means 'our' when joined to a noun. The genitive here is governed by the preposition.

25.meaning: A verb meaning 'they knowingly reject / deny / repudiate.' Its distinctive sense is denying something one inwardly recognizes to be true — rejection against better knowledge.

parts.en: they (the prefix marking a third-person subject)
plural marker, with the -na of the ongoing/present

25.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, third-person masculine plural. The ya- prefix marks 'they,' and -ūna marks a plural subject and an ongoing or repeated action. The retained -na is the mark of the indicative mood, the verb's default unbroken form.
25.root: ج-ح-د (j-ḥ-d) — to deny or reject what one knows to be true

1.meaning: So We sent / dispatched — to send forth a messenger, a message, or (as here) something loosed upon people. The form has the subject 'we'.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the form IV pattern (arsala, 'to send'), with the attached subject pronoun -nā ('we'). The fa- prefix marks consequence or sequence ('so, then'). The -nā ending shows that 'we' performed the completed action.

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
2.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: a wind / a (dry, blighting) wind
3.grammar: noun, feminine, indefinite, accusative — rīḥ (singular) used here for a specific wind, contrasted with the life-giving plural riyāḥ; the -an tanwīn marks it as indefinite and accusative; a single wind can be a sign of destruction or hardship (as when it turns the crops yellow)
3.root: ر-و-ح (r-w-ḥ) — wind, breath; rīḥ: a wind

4.meaning: furious
4.grammar: See Arabic text.

5.meaning: The preposition 'in / within / during.' It places something inside a container, period, place, or matter.
5.grammar: A preposition. It governs the noun that follows, putting it in the genitive case and situating something inside it — in space, in time ('during'), or in a circumstance.

6.meaning: Days — the plural of 'day,' periods of daylight or twenty-four-hour spans.
6.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of yawm ('day'). The ending -in (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('days') and in the genitive case, the form used in a possessive link ('… of days') or after a preposition.
6.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time

7.meaning: Ill-fated / inauspicious / disastrous — bringing misfortune, calamity, and ruin; describing days or things laden with bad fortune.
7.grammar: A feminine sound-plural adjective ('ill-omened, disastrous'). The ending -in (tanwīn kasra) is indefinite and, for this plural type, serves as both genitive and accusative — used after prepositions, for possession, or as an object — describing an unspecified plural (e.g. 'days') as bringers of misfortune.

8.meaning: A purpose-clause verb meaning 'so that We may make them taste'. Built on the causative verb 'to make someone taste/experience', it frames an intended outcome: causing a group to actually undergo and feel something (often a punishment or consequence), as vividly as one tastes food. The opening particle marks this as the goal or reason behind a prior action.

parts.en: so that / in order that (purpose lām with assimilated 'an')

8.grammar: The prefixed لِّ (li-) is the lām of purpose, 'so that / in order that'. It carries a shaddah (gemination) because an implicit particle 'an' ('that') is absorbed into it: the nūn of that 'an' assimilates into the lām, doubling it (li- + an → li-). This hidden 'an' is exactly what drives the verb into the subjunctive. The نُ (nu-) prefix marks a 'we' subject in the non-past. The verb is causative (Form IV: 'to make someone taste'). The final -a is the subjunctive mood, which appears after such purpose constructions, showing the action is intended/dependent rather than a standalone statement. The attached -hum means 'them' as the object.

9.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
9.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

10.meaning: the disgrace / humiliation — a state of being brought low, shamed, and degraded; abasement and ignominy.
10.grammar: A definite noun ('the disgrace'), marked by the prefixed al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, which typically links the noun to a preceding one ('the … OF …') or follows a preposition. It names the abstract state of being disgraced.
10.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — to be disgraced, humiliated, put to shame

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
12.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.
12.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, being alive, living

13.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
13.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
13.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

14.meaning: Severe suffering, torment, or punishment inflicted as chastisement. The prefixes add emphasis and definiteness: 'and surely the punishment …'.
14.grammar: A noun with the -u (nominative) ending, the case used for a sentence's subject. The la- prefix is an emphatic 'surely/indeed', and wa- is 'and'. Together: 'and surely the punishment …'.
14.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish, cause pain

15.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
15.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
15.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

16.meaning: An elative adjective meaning 'more/most disgracing' or 'more humiliating'. From a root about being put to shame and disgraced, it describes something that brings a greater degree of public humiliation and abasement than something else.
16.grammar: This is the elative (afʿal) pattern, which expresses 'more …' or 'most …' — here 'more disgracing/humiliating'. The word ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) and does not take the usual short case-vowels; this invariable ending is characteristic of this adjective shape. It conveys a comparative/superlative degree of the quality of disgrace.
16.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — disgrace, humiliation, being put to shame

17.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
17.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.

18.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
18.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

19.meaning: To be helped, aided, or given victory — for support to be granted, especially against an adversary.
19.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, masculine plural 'they.' The yu- prefix is the third-person masculine imperfect marker; the passive sense ('they are being helped,' by an unnamed helper) comes from the internal vowelling rather than from the prefix itself. The -ūna ending marks a plural subject in the plain (indicative) present, used for an ongoing or general fact.
19.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, grant victory

1.meaning: 'And as for …' A connective that introduces and sets apart a new topic for separate comment, usually anticipating a matching response clause. The 'and' joins it on; 'ammā' means 'as for (such-and-such)…'
1.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā singles out a topic for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that supplies the comment. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: 'Thamūd' — the proper name of an ancient Arabian people to whom the prophet Ṣāliḥ was sent.
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -u is nominative, the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being described. As a tribal proper name it is a 'diptote' and so does not take the indefinite -n ending.
2.root: — (proper name)

3.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'We guided them' — to show the right way, lead onto a straight path, or direct toward correct belief and conduct. The root carries the sense of giving guidance as a gift.
3.grammar: The prefixed فَ (fa-) means 'so/then' and links to what precedes. The verb is past tense. The suffix -nā attached to a past-tense verb marks the subject 'we' (the doers). The further attached -hum is the object 'them'. So the form packs subject and object onto one past verb: 'we guided them'.

4.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'they preferred / they chose (something) in love over (something else)'. Built on a Form X pattern of the root for 'love', it means to deliberately favour and embrace one thing in preference to another, treating it as more beloved.
4.grammar: The prefixed فَ (fa-) connects to what precedes ('so/but'). The stem is Form X (ista- pattern) of the root for love, giving the sense of seeking/choosing what one loves, hence 'to prefer'. The past-tense ending -ū marks a masculine plural 'they' subject (the silent alif written after it is just spelling). It states a completed choice made by a group.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'blindness' — the inability to see. It is commonly used both literally and figuratively for the loss of inner sight: failure to perceive truth or guidance.
5.grammar: The prefixed ٱلۡ (al-) is the definite article 'the'. The noun ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) and is invariable, so it does not display the usual short case-endings. It names the state/quality of being blind.

6.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
6.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
6.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

7.meaning: The guidance; the right leading and true direction (with the definite article, 'the Guidance').
7.grammar: A definite verbal noun: the prefix al- means 'the'. It ends in a long -ā (from a weak-final root), an ending that does not change for case. It denotes the abstract reality of right guidance, made specific and definite by 'the'.
7.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

8.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'so it seized them / took hold of them'. From a root about grasping and taking, it conveys something gripping or overtaking a group suddenly and forcefully (often a punishment).
8.grammar: The prefixed فَ (fa-) means 'so/then'. The verb is past tense. The -t ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it' did it), which agrees with a grammatically feminine doer. The attached -hum is the object 'them'. Together: 'so it (fem.) seized them'.

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'a thunderbolt' or 'a stunning blast' — a sudden, overwhelming strike (a lightning-bolt, a deafening cry, or a shock that fells or stuns). From a root about being struck senseless.
9.grammar: This is an active-participle-shaped feminine noun (the ة / -a is the feminine ending). The final short -u is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject/doer of a sentence or simply named as such. It denotes the striking thing itself.

10.meaning: The punishment, torment, or chastisement — severe penalty or suffering inflicted as retribution.
10.grammar: A singular masculine noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending is the genitive, which typically links it to a preceding noun ('… of the punishment') or follows a preposition.
10.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment

11.meaning: The disgrace / humiliation / abasement — a noun naming the state of being lowered and dishonoured, the opposite of honour and might. Carries the definite article 'the'.
11.grammar: A definite noun (with 'al-', 'the'). The final -i (kasra) is genitive: it marks the word as linked to a preceding preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to another noun.
11.root: ه-و-ن (h-w-n) — lowliness, disgrace, being held cheap

12.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
12.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

13.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
13.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

14.meaning: They earn / acquire — to gain, accumulate, or bring upon oneself something through one's own effort or action, whether wealth, deeds, or their consequences (good or bad).
14.grammar: Present-tense verb. The 'ya-' prefix together with the '-ūna' ending marks 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or habitually. The full '-ūna' (rather than shortened '-ū') signals the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact, not a command or subjunctive.

1.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'and We saved/delivered/rescued'. Built on an intensive (Form II) pattern, it stresses bringing someone safely out of danger or destruction.
1.grammar: The prefixed وَ (wa-) means 'and'. The doubled middle consonant marks Form II, giving an intensive/causative sense ('to bring to safety'). The verb is past tense, and the suffix -nā marks the 'we' subject who performed it. So: 'and we delivered/saved'.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

5.meaning: They are mindful of Allah / they guard themselves; to live in reverent awareness that shields one from wrongdoing (the verb behind taqwā).
5.grammar: A Form VIII present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they (do)' for a group of males, with the final -na marking the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing or habitual reality.
5.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to protect, shield, guard against harm

1.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
1.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

2.meaning: A present/future passive verb meaning 'is/will be gathered together' — to be collected and assembled into one place, as a crowd or multitude is mustered.
2.grammar: The يُ (yu-) prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks a masculine singular passive in the non-past: the subject is acted upon, not acting ('is gathered'). The final -u is the indicative mood, the default ending for a plain, ongoing/future statement (not commanded or made dependent). It points to an act of assembling done to someone.
2.root: ح-ش-ر (ḥ-sh-r) — gathering, mustering a crowd

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'enemies / foes' — the plural of 'enemy', those in hostility and opposition. From a root about transgression and overstepping into hostility.
3.grammar: This is a broken (irregular) plural meaning 'enemies'. The final short -u is the nominative case, used when the noun is the subject/doer or is simply named. Because it is a noun that links to a following word, it often heads a possessive phrase, 'the enemies OF …'.

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
5.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

6.meaning: 'The Fire' — fire, flame; in religious usage often the Fire of Hell, the blazing punishment of the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article 'al-' ('the') plus the feminine noun 'nār' ('fire'). The 'l' of 'al-' assimilates into the following 'n' (so it is pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-i' ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or to link the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the Fire').
6.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze, burning

7.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
7.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

8.meaning: A present/future passive verb meaning 'they are/will be marshalled in ranks' — to be driven and arranged into ordered rows, with the foremost held back so the whole group is kept together and aligned.
8.grammar: This is a non-past passive (Form I): the subjects are acted upon, not acting. The root is و-ز-ع, whose first radical is a wāw. When the passive prefix yu- meets that wāw, the two merge: the short ḍamma of yu- combines with the wāw into a single long ū, giving yū- at the start (yu- + w → yū-). This contraction is why the form opens with a long ū that belongs partly to the prefix and partly to the first radical, and cannot be split cleanly between them. The ending -ūna marks a masculine plural subject 'they' and is the indicative mood — the full -na shows a plain, ongoing/future statement rather than a dependent or commanded one. So: 'they are being arranged/held in ranks'.
8.root: و-ز-ع (w-z-ʿ) — restraining and marshalling into order

1.meaning: A particle meaning 'until / up to the point that / so that finally'. It marks an end-limit in time or place, or the goal at which an action culminates.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case endings and never changes form). It introduces the end-point or purpose of what precedes, and when followed by a verb it can give the sense of 'until' or 'so that'.

2.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
2.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

4.meaning: They reach it / when they come to it — jāūhā means 'they came to it', 'they arrived at it', describing the disbelievers arriving at Hell.

parts.en: they came, they arrived (third masculine plural perfect)
it (feminine pronoun — referring to Jahannam/Hell, which is treated as feminine)

4.grammar: Jāū is Form I perfect (third masculine plural) from root j-y-ʾ/j-w-ʾ. The suffix -hā is the third-person feminine pronoun referring to Jahannam (Hell). Context: 'until when they reach it (jāūhā), its gates will be opened' — describing the moment the disbelievers arrive at the gates of Hell.

5.meaning: He witnessed, bore witness, or was present — to observe something directly and so be able to testify to it, or simply to be present for it.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular. The final -a marks a completed act done by 'he' ('he witnessed / was present').
5.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

6.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
6.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
6.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'their hearing' — the faculty of hearing, the sense by which sounds are perceived, belonging to a group.
7.grammar: The core noun means 'hearing'. The short -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, marking the noun as the subject/doer. The attached -hum means 'their' (a masculine-plural possessor), so the whole is 'their hearing'.

8.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'and their sight / their eyes' — the plural of the faculty of seeing (vision), or the eyes themselves, belonging to a group.
8.grammar: The prefixed وَ (wa-) means 'and'. The noun is a broken plural of 'sight/eye'. The short -u before the pronoun is the nominative case (subject/doer). The attached -hum means 'their' (masculine plural). So: 'and their sights/eyes'.

9.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'and their skins' — the plural of 'skin', the outer covering of the body, belonging to a group.
9.grammar: The prefixed وَ (wa-) means 'and'. The noun is a broken plural of 'skin'. The short -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, marking it as subject/doer. The attached -hum means 'their' (masculine plural). So: 'and their skins'.

10.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
10.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

11.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
11.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

12.meaning: 'They do / they work / they act' — to perform deeds or carry out actions, ongoing or habitual.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks third-person masculine plural ('they do/work'). The retained final -na (the 'ūna' ending) is the indicative form, used for a plain, ongoing, or habitual action that is simply being stated.
12.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
1.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

2.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'to their skins' — directed toward the skins (the body's outer covering) of a group. The opening particle marks the skins as the addressee or recipient of an action (e.g. of speech directed at them).
2.grammar: The prefixed لِ (li-) means 'to/for' and directs the action toward something. After this preposition the noun takes the genitive case, here shown by the -i vowel before the pronoun — the regular ending a noun takes when governed by a preposition. The attached pronoun appears as -him ('their', masculine plural), its vowel harmonising with the preceding -i. So: 'to their skins'.
2.root: ج-ل-د (j-l-d) — skin, hide

3.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'why? / for what reason?' — a question asking the cause or purpose of something. It is formed from the preposition 'for/about' fused with the question-word 'what'.
3.grammar: A question particle built from li- ('for, about') joined to mā ('what'); when these combine, the long vowel of 'what' is shortened to give li-ma ('for what?, why?'). It opens a question seeking a reason or motive.

4.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'you (all) testified / bore witness'. From the root for witnessing, it means a group affirmed and gave testimony to something they directly knew or observed.
4.grammar: The verb is past tense, from the root for bearing witness. The ending -tum marks the subject 'you (plural)' — a group of addressees who did the action (the doubled t arises as the stem's final د meets the t of the suffix). So: 'you all testified'.

5.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
5.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

6.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

7.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'made us speak / caused us to talk'. Built on a causative (Form IV) pattern of the root for speech, it means to give the power of speech or compel utterance from someone.
7.grammar: The verb is past tense in the causative Form IV (the أ a- prefix on the root gives 'to make/cause to …'), so 'to make speak'. The final -a is the standard past-tense ending for a 'he/it' subject. The attached -nā is the object 'us'. So: 'he/it made us speak'.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: A relative pronoun, masculine singular, meaning 'who / which / the one that.' It links a following clause to a noun, marking it out as 'the [noun] that…'
9.grammar: A masculine-singular relative pronoun. It is indeclinable (its form does not change for case) and introduces a description, equivalent to 'the one who/which…'

10.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'made (someone) speak / caused to speak'. The same causative (Form IV) verb of the root for speech, denoting granting the ability to speak or drawing forth speech.
10.grammar: This is the causative Form IV of the root for speech: the initial أَ (a-) prefix on the root turns 'to speak' into 'to make/cause to speak'. The final -a is the regular past-tense ending for a masculine singular 'he/it' subject, isolated here as the inflection on the verb stem. With no attached object pronoun, the object is left to be supplied separately. So: 'he/it made (someone) speak'.
10.root: ن-ط-ق (n-ṭ-q) — speech, articulate utterance

11.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
11.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.
11.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — wholeness, totality

12.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
12.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
12.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

13.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
13.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

14.meaning: 'He created you' — He brought you into existence, originating and shaping you. The verb denotes bringing something into being and giving it its form and proportion, here with 'you (plural)' as the one(s) created.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb with an attached object pronoun. The stem is the three root letters; the '-a' ending on it marks 'he' as the doer in the completed past ('he created'). The suffix '-kum' is the object 'you (plural),' i.e. the ones to whom the action was done.

15.meaning: First, foremost — the one that comes before all others in time, order, or rank.
15.grammar: A noun/adjective meaning 'first', here in a form that does not take normal indefinite case-tanwīn (a 'diptote'). The -a ending is accusative, marking it as an object or, very often, as the leading term of a possessive phrase ('the first of …').
15.root: أ-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to return to a beginning

16.meaning: One time / once / an instance — a noun denoting a single occurrence of an act. Indefinite ('a time'), as shown by its two-vowel (tanwin) ending.
16.grammar: A feminine noun meaning 'a single time/occurrence'. The doubled-vowel ending (tanwin, here -in) marks it as indefinite ('a time', not 'the time'); the -i quality of that ending is genitive, signalling the word follows a preposition or links to another noun. It often expresses 'one time / once'.
16.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — passing by; an instance or occurrence of something

17.meaning: And to Him / toward Him. The wa- means 'and'; ilā is the preposition 'to/toward' indicating direction or destination; the attached pronoun -hi means 'him'.
17.grammar: Wa- means 'and'. Ilā ('to/toward') is a preposition of direction; it takes the special form 'ilay-' before a pronoun. The attached -hi is the genitive pronoun 'him', the form pronouns take after prepositions; the -i vowel reflects that genitive attachment.

18.meaning: 'You are returned / brought back' — a passive verb from the root meaning to return: the subjects are made to go back, sent back to a point of origin, the action being done to them rather than by them.
18.grammar: Present/future passive. The tu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'), and the internal vowelling (u–a) makes it passive — the action is done TO the subject. The -ūna ending is the full ('indicative') plural form, used when the verb is not cut short by certain particles.

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
2.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. As the doer is built into the suffix, the verb itself is in its base past form ('you all were').
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

3.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'you (all) conceal/hide yourselves' or 'screen yourselves'. Built on a reflexive (Form VIII) pattern of the root for covering/veiling, it means a group screens or shields itself from view or from being detected.
3.grammar: The تَ (ta-) prefix marks a 'you' subject in the non-past. The stem is reflexive Form VIII of the root for covering, so the action folds back on the doer ('to cover/screen oneself'). The ending -ūna marks a masculine plural 'you' and is the indicative mood — the full -na shows a plain, ongoing/future statement. So: 'you (all) screen yourselves'.

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning '(that) it bear witness / testify'. From the root for witnessing, it denotes giving testimony or affirming what one knows or has observed.
5.grammar: The يَ (ya-) prefix marks a masculine singular 'he/it' subject in the non-past. The final -a here is the subjunctive mood, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that / so that / lest' and shows the action is dependent or anticipated rather than a flat statement. So: '(that) he/it testify'.

6.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
6.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.
6.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: A noun meaning 'your hearing' — the faculty of hearing belonging to a group of addressees.
7.grammar: The core noun means 'hearing'. The short -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, marking the noun as subject/doer. The attached -kum means 'your' addressed to a group ('you all'). So: 'your hearing'.

8.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
8.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'your sight / your eyes' — the plural of the faculty of seeing, or the eyes, belonging to a group of addressees.
9.grammar: The noun is a broken plural of 'sight/eye'. The short -u before the pronoun is the nominative case (subject/doer). The attached -kum means 'your' addressed to a group. So: 'your sights/eyes'.

10.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
10.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

11.meaning: A noun meaning 'your skins' — the plural of 'skin', the body's outer covering, belonging to a group of addressees.
11.grammar: The noun is a broken plural of 'skin'. The short -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, marking it as subject/doer. The attached -kum means 'your' addressed to a group. So: 'your skins'.
11.root: ج-ل-د (j-l-d) — skin, hide

12.meaning: 'But / however / yet' — a particle of correction and contrast that sets aside what came before and affirms something different instead.
12.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to lākin ('but / however'). Lākin is a particle of rectification: it draws a contrast with, or corrects, the preceding idea and introduces an opposing or qualifying statement ('... but rather...').

13.meaning: You (plural) thought / you assumed — past tense, 2nd person plural: the belief or assumption held by those being addressed. In context, refers to the false assumption that the Prophet would not return from Hudaybiyyah.

parts.en: you (pl.) thought / assumed (2nd masc. pl. past)

13.grammar: Past tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural, Form I. A doubled root (ظ-ن-ن) with assimilation of the doubled nūn.
13.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, to assume; often with a sense of conjecture or false belief

14.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
14.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

15.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
15.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

16.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
16.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

17.meaning: 'He/it knows' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have knowledge of, be aware of, recognize, or understand something.
17.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The ya- prefix marks 'he,' and the final -u marks the ordinary (indicative) present, 'he knows / does know.'
17.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge; knowing, being aware, recognizing

18.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
18.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (the 'tanwīn' of fatḥa). The accusative case here commonly marks an object of a verb or an indefinite quantity; the doubled-n sound (nunation) signals that the word is indefinite ('many', not 'the many').
18.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

19.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
19.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

20.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
20.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'and that' — pointing to something distant or already mentioned, while specifically addressing a group of people ('that, which concerns you all').
1.grammar: The prefixed وَ (wa-) means 'and'. The base ذَا (dhā) is the demonstrative 'that', pointing to something far off or previously referenced. The -kum ending is a second-person plural addressee marker ('you all'), tuning the demonstrative to a plural audience — so the whole conveys 'that (over there), O you'. It is an indeclinable pointing-word, so it does not change for case.

2.meaning: Your supposition, conjecture, or assumption — what you (a group) think or presume to be the case, often a belief held without certain knowledge. This noun denotes an opinion or expectation that may or may not correspond to reality.
2.grammar: A noun carrying an attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your', addressing more than one). The -u vowel on the stem is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject or the thing being identified. The final vowel on -kumu appears as -u (rather than -ū) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting sound.
2.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, conjecture, think (without certainty)

3.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
3.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

4.meaning: You (plural) thought / you assumed — past tense, 2nd person plural: the belief or assumption held by those being addressed. In context, refers to the false assumption that the Prophet would not return from Hudaybiyyah.

parts.en: you (pl.) thought / assumed (2nd masc. pl. past)

4.grammar: Past tense verb, 2nd person masculine plural, Form I. A doubled root (ظ-ن-ن) with assimilation of the doubled nūn.
4.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to think, to assume; often with a sense of conjecture or false belief

5.meaning: 'By/in your Lord' — combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the noun 'Lord' (the Master, Sustainer, and Nurturer who owns, provides for, and brings to maturity) with the pronoun 'your (plural)'.
5.grammar: A preposition attached to a noun carrying a possessive pronoun. The preposition bi- ('with/by/in') puts the noun into the genitive case, reflected in the -i vowel of rabbi. The suffix -kum means 'your' addressing a plural group.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

6.meaning: It brought you (a group) to ruin, destroyed you, or cast you into perdition — a completed action of leading someone to their downfall or doom.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person singular ('it/he did'), built on the causative pattern (af'ala) which adds the sense of 'to make fall into ruin.' It carries the attached object pronoun -kum, 'you all,' marking the group as the ones acted upon. The verb itself stands as a completed act.
6.root: ر-د-ي (r-d-y) — to perish, fall to destruction; (causative) to ruin

7.meaning: Then you (plural) became, came to be, ended up in a new state — originally 'to enter the morning', widely used to mean simply 'to become'.
7.grammar: The connector 'then/so' attached to a past-tense verb with the ending -tum, which marks 'you all' (masculine plural) as the doers of a completed action. This verb belongs to the family of 'becoming' verbs: it reports a change of state and normally introduces a description of what the people became.
7.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning, daybreak; to come to be

8.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
8.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

9.meaning: "The losers / those who lose" — an active participle for those who suffer loss, who lose out or come to ruin, especially the ultimate loss of one's own soul.
9.grammar: An active participle in the masculine sound plural with the definite article 'the'. The -īna ending marks the accusative or genitive case — the form used when such a plural is a direct object, a predicate of 'to be', or follows a preposition (as opposed to the -ūna subject form).
9.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose / suffer loss / be ruined

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

2.meaning: They show patience, endure, bear steadfastly, or restrain themselves — to hold firm under hardship without collapsing or complaining.
2.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third person masculine plural. The ya- prefix together with the -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group). The bare -ū ending (rather than -ūna) shows the verb is in a 'cut-short' mood — the form it takes after certain particles such as conditionals or negatives, which drop the final -na.
2.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — patience, steadfast endurance, self-restraint

3.meaning: Then the Fire — the connective 'then/so' joined to 'the Fire' (chiefly the fire of Hell, the punishment of the next life).
3.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') prefixed to a definite feminine noun, 'the Fire' (with 'al-' assimilated into the 'n' sound, pronounced 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case marking a subject or the thing being identified — often the answer-clause introduced by 'fa'.
3.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, light, to give light

4.meaning: An abode / a dwelling place — mathwan is a noun meaning a dwelling, a resting place, or an abode — here referring to Hell as the dwelling of the liars.

parts.en: a dwelling, an abode, a resting place

4.grammar: Mathwā is a Form I noun of place (mafʿal pattern) from root th-w-y, meaning a place of staying or dwelling. In the indefinite accusative (tanwīn fatḥa -an). The verse: 'Is there not in Hell an abode (mathwan) for the arrogant?' — rhetorically affirming the punishment awaiting them.
4.root: ث-و-ي (th-w-y) — to stay, to dwell, to reside; a dwelling place

5.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
5.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

6.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
6.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

7.meaning: They seek to please, ask to be allowed to make amends, or plead for the chance to return to favor — to request that one's apology or repentance be accepted so that goodwill is restored.

parts.en: seek to make amends / win back favor

7.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third person masculine plural, built on the 'seeking' pattern (istaf'ala) which adds the sense of asking for or trying to obtain something — here, the restoration of favor. The ya-…-ū frame marks 'they'; the short -ū ending (not -ūna) shows the cut-short mood used after particles like negatives or conditionals.
7.root: ع-ت-ب (ʿ-t-b) — to reproach; (in this pattern) to seek reconciliation and the lifting of reproach

8.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
8.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

9.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
9.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

10.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
10.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

11.meaning: Those who are granted satisfaction and have their plea accepted — people permitted to return to favor and reconciliation, with the cause of reproach lifted from them. A definite plural noun naming such persons.

parts.en: one granted satisfaction / whose reproach is lifted

11.grammar: A passive participle (the one to whom an action is done) of the causative pattern (af'ala, here the muf'al shape muʿtab — note the single t), so it names the one who is granted satisfaction and has reproach lifted from him, not the one who does so. It is made definite by the prefix al- ('the') and plural by the ending -īna. The -īna marks a masculine 'sound plural' in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state — the form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition, as opposed to -ūna for the subject form.
11.root: ع-ت-ب (ʿ-t-b) — reproach; (causative) to grant satisfaction and lift reproach after estrangement

1.meaning: And We assigned, appointed, or destined — a completed act of arranging or sending something to take charge of or attach itself to someone. The doubled middle consonant intensifies the sense of deliberate appointing.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive pattern (faʿʿala, with a doubled middle letter) prefixed by 'and' (wa-) and ending in -nā, 'we.' The -nā suffix names the doers as 'we' and marks the verb as a completed action.
1.root: ق-ي-ض (q-y-ḍ) — to allot, appoint, prepare and set over

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: Companions, close associates, or comrades — those who are paired or yoked with another, accompanying them constantly. A plural noun for inseparable companions or counterparts.
3.grammar: A broken plural (singular qarīn, 'companion') on the fuʿalā' pattern, which is a diptote — a noun barred from full inflection. The -a ending here is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). Because it is a diptote, this same -a (with no tanwīn) also serves as its genitive ending: such nouns do not take the -i (kasra) that ordinary nouns use after a preposition or in a possessive link. It names those who are joined or paired with someone.
3.root: ق-ر-ن (q-r-n) — to join, couple, pair together; a companion

4.meaning: So they made (something) seem attractive, beautified it, or dressed it up to appear pleasing — a completed act of adorning or making appealing, often deceptively. The doubled middle consonant gives the sense of actively decorating.
4.grammar: A past-tense verb in the intensive pattern (faʿʿala, doubled middle letter), prefixed by fa- ('so/then,' often signaling a result or sequence) and ending in -ū, the marker for 'they' (masculine plural). The verb stands as a completed action done by a group.
4.root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n) — adornment, beautification, making something attractive

5.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
5.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

6.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
6.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
6.root: — (particle; no root)

7.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
7.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

8.meaning: Their hands. The plural noun 'hands' carrying the masculine plural possessive 'their'; often used idiomatically for what people do, produce, or are responsible for through their own deeds.
8.grammar: A plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-him' meaning 'their' (a group of males, or mixed). 'aydī' is the irregular ('broken') plural of 'yad' (hand). The pronoun ending makes the whole construction definite and possessed; the 'i'-coloured stem before the suffix reflects its genitive/possessed state, the form typically following a preposition or standing as object.

9.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

10.meaning: 'behind them' — the space or position to the rear of a group; also figuratively what lies after them, what awaits them, or what is hidden from them.
10.grammar: An adverb of place ('behind') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The -a ending is accusative, the case regularly used for adverbs of place and time, indicating the location 'behind.'
10.root: خ-ل-ف (kh-l-f) — to be behind, come after, succeed

11.meaning: And it became due, was rightly established, came true, or was justly confirmed — a completed action meaning a statement, verdict, or consequence has been proven right and rightfully takes effect.

parts.en: became due / was confirmed as true

11.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('it/he'), prefixed by 'and' (wa-). The final -a is the standard ending of such a past verb. The root meaning of truth and rightful due gives the verb the force of something being justly established or coming to pass as deserved.
11.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, what is rightfully due and established

12.meaning: 'Upon them / against them' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, against') carrying an attached plural pronoun referring to a group of males.
12.grammar: ʿalā ('upon') takes the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The -him ending is the attached pronoun for a masculine plural 'them'; its final vowel appears as -u (himu) to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with the definite article.

13.meaning: The word, the saying, the utterance — a statement or pronouncement; qawl is speech that has been spoken, and 'the word' can mean a settled decree or verdict.
13.grammar: A definite noun ('the …'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
13.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; a saying, statement, or pronouncement.

14.meaning: The preposition 'in / within / during.' It places something inside a container, period, place, or matter.
14.grammar: A preposition. It governs the noun that follows, putting it in the genitive case and situating something inside it — in space, in time ('during'), or in a circumstance.

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'nations, communities, or peoples' — the plural of 'umma,' a group bound together as one community.
15.grammar: A plural noun. The ending -in is genitive and indefinite (the doubled 'nunation' marking 'some, an indefinite'). The genitive case typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding noun (the 'of' relationship), and the -in shows it is indefinite ('some communities').

16.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
16.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

17.meaning: 'It passed away / went by, came to an end' — said of a community, time, or era that has elapsed and is now gone. The root carries the sense of being emptied out, hence of time or people that have passed.
17.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -t (sukūn-marked -at) suffix marks a third-person feminine singular subject, 'she/it,' used here because the noun it refers to is grammatically feminine. The past tense states a completed action.
17.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty/vacant; to pass away, elapse

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
19.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
19.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

20.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
20.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

21.meaning: A noun meaning 'the jinn' — a class of unseen beings created from smokeless fire, possessing free will and accountability like humankind.
21.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- ('the'). The -i (genitive) ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in a possessive 'of' relationship.
21.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, be hidden from sight

22.meaning: And humankind — human beings collectively, mankind, especially as contrasted with the unseen jinn. Carries a sense of sociability and familiarity.
22.grammar: A collective noun with the prefixed 'and' plus 'the'. The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically follows a preposition or oath particle, or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.

23.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
23.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

24.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
24.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
24.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

25.meaning: Losers — those who suffer loss and ruin, ending up with a deficit. A 'khāsir' is one whose venture or final account comes out at a loss.
25.grammar: An active participle (one in the state of the action) in the masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the accusative/genitive plural — used for a direct object, after a preposition, or (as often here) describing a state, e.g. 'as losers'.

1.meaning: 'And he said' — the act of speaking or stating, attributed to one masculine speaker, joined to what precedes by 'and.'
1.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') with a past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he said.' The ending -a marks a completed action by one male, with the doer 'he' contained in the verb.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: You (a group) listen, hear, or pay heed — to take in sound with attention. The verb covers both the bare act of hearing and the fuller sense of heeding what is heard.
5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb addressed to a group, second person masculine plural ('you all'). The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks this 'you-plural.' The short -ū (not -ūna) shows the cut-short mood the verb takes after certain particles such as negatives or conditionals.

6.meaning: For this / to this — the preposition 'for, to' attached to the near demonstrative 'this', pointing to something close at hand or just mentioned, and assigning it as goal or beneficiary.
6.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to', indicating purpose, direction, or benefit) prefixed to the masculine singular near-demonstrative 'hādhā' ('this'). Demonstratives are indeclinable, so their ending does not change for case.

7.meaning: The Qur'an — the recited Revelation; literally 'the Recitation/Reading,' the Book sent down to be recited aloud.
7.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'recitation/reading,' used as the proper name of the Book, with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive ending: it typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').

8.meaning: And make a clamor, raise noise, talk over (something), or babble loudly — a command to a group to drown out or disrupt with confused, raised voices. Carries the sense of meaningless or distracting din.
8.grammar: A Form I (faʿala) imperative addressed to a group of males ('you all do this'), prefixed by 'and' (wa-), from a final-weak (defective) root. The leading ٱ is a connecting (waṣl) alif that the basic imperative needs in order to be pronounceable — it is sounded only when the word begins an utterance and elides after wa-; it is NOT the definite article 'the.'
