14.grammar: A singular noun denoting a female. It ends in a fixed long -ā that does not change for case, so its grammatical role is shown by context rather than by a final vowel.

15.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

16.meaning: Gives birth / lays down / delivers — the act of giving birth or bearing young. Also used for the act of setting something down or depositing a load, from the same root of 'putting down a burden'.

parts.en: she (3rd person feminine singular imperfect prefix)
puts down / gives birth (stem from the root 'to place/deliver')

16.grammar: Taḍaʿu is an imperfect (present/future) verb, 3rd person feminine singular — the ta- prefix marks the feminine singular or 2nd person masculine, but contextually here it is 3rd person feminine ('she'). The stem is from waḍaʿa (to put down, to give birth). The -u ending is the standard imperfect indicative ending ('she does / she is doing'). The dropping of the initial wāw of the root is a regular feature of waaw-initial (mithāl) verbs in the imperfect.
16.root: و-ض-ع (w-ḍ-ʿ) — to put down, to place, to give birth

17.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
17.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

18.meaning: 'with His knowledge' — by means of, or accompanied by, Allah's own knowledge.
18.grammar: The prefix bi- ('with / by means of') is a preposition. The base is 'knowledge,' and the attached -hi means 'His.' The -i ending on the noun is genitive, the case required after the preposition bi-.

19.meaning: "and (on the) day" — the conjunction "and" joined to the noun for "day," a single daytime period or, more broadly, an appointed day or time of judgment/event.
19.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction "and." The -a ending on the noun is accusative; on a word for "day" this frequently marks it as an adverb of time ("on the day …"), or marks it as the object of a verb.

20.meaning: He will call them / He will summon them. Refers to the divine act of calling out to people on the Day of Judgement — addressing them with a question or announcement.

parts.en: He calls, He summons, He calls out to (Form III, present 3rd masculine singular)
them (3rd person masculine plural object pronoun)

20.grammar: Present-tense verb (mudāriʿ), 3rd person masculine singular, Form III (nādā — to call out to). The -ī is the stem ending of this hollow verb; -him is the plural object pronoun.
20.root: ن-د-و/ي (n-d-w/y) — to call; Form III: to call out to, to summon

21.meaning: Where / wherever. An interrogative or conditional adverb of place: it asks 'where?' or, in a conditional sense, sets up 'wherever / in whatever place'.
21.grammar: An indeclinable adverb of place fixed on a final -a; it does not change for case. It functions either as a question word ('where?') or as a conditional particle introducing a clause ('wherever'), often pairing with a following verb in the jussive mood.

22.meaning: My partners / my associates — those who have been associated with someone as partners or equals; in theological contexts, referring to alleged partners attributed to Allah, i.e., false deities or associates claimed to share in His divinity.

parts.en: my (1st person singular possessive pronoun, genitive)

22.grammar: Shurakāʾ is the broken plural of sharīk (partner, associate). The -ī suffix is the 1st person singular possessive pronoun 'my', which attaches in the genitive, converting the noun to 'my partners'. The final hamza of the plural merges with the yāʾ of the pronoun. Genitive possession is the standard function of attached pronouns on nouns.
22.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, to associate, to be a partner; shirk is the act of associating others with Allah

23.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.

24.meaning: We announce to you / We give notice to you / We have declared to you — the act of making a formal or solemn announcement or declaration to a listener.

parts.en: we have announced / we declare (Form IV perfect verb, 1st person plural)
to you (2nd person masculine singular object pronoun)

24.grammar: Ādhannā is a perfect (past or timeless) verb in Form IV (afʿala), 1st person plural — the -nā suffix marks 'we'. Form IV of this root means 'to announce, to inform, to give notice'. The shadda (gemination) on the nūn arises because the final root consonant of the root ʾ-dh-n (the nūn) immediately precedes the nūn of the first-person plural suffix -nā, causing the two identical consonants to merge into a single geminated nūn. The attached -ka is the 2nd person masculine singular object pronoun 'you (singular)'. The perfect can express a solemn declaration that stands as completed fact.
24.root: أ-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — to permit; to call; to announce; the ear (udhun) and hence 'to make someone's ear aware'

25.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
25.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

26.meaning: "from us" — the preposition 'from' (indicating origin, source, or starting point) fused with the attached pronoun 'us'. It can also carry a partitive sense, 'some of us / a part of us'.
26.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The base 'min' normally takes a vowelless final consonant, but before the pronoun '-nā' the nūn is doubled (assimilation), giving 'minnā'. The suffix '-nā' is the first-person plural object/possessive pronoun meaning 'us' or 'our'.
26.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

27.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
27.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

28.meaning: A witness — one who witnesses, testifies, or bears evidence; one who is present and aware of events, or who testifies on behalf of or against someone. As a divine name it means the All-Witnessing.

parts.en: witness / one who testifies (intensive participial adjective)

28.grammar: Shahīd is in the faʿīl pattern, which in Arabic can mean the one who is thoroughly characterized by the root action — hence 'an ever-present witness' or 'one who is inherently witnessing'. The -in ending (tanwīn kasra) marks it as indefinite and genitive, typically following a preposition or appearing as the second term in a possessive (iḍāfa) chain.
28.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, to be present, to testify

1.meaning: "And it went astray / was lost / went to ruin." A past-tense verb meaning that something strayed from the right path, missed its target, or vanished and came to nothing. The opening wa- adds "and."
1.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb in the "he/it" third-person masculine singular form. With no subject pronoun attached, the bare verb itself carries the sense "he/it strayed."
1.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, be lost, err

2.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
2.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.
2.root: — (a preposition; no triliteral verbal root)

3.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
3.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

4.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
4.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

5.meaning: 'They call / invite / summon' — to call upon, invite, or summon (also to pray to or call out to); a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
5.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they call/invite'). The ya- prefix with the full -ūna ending marks 'they (men) do' and shows the indicative mood — the plain statement form ('they do'), with its final nūn intact (contrast the jussive/subjunctive, where it drops).
5.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
6.root: — (preposition)

7.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
7.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
7.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

8.meaning: And they became convinced or sure, reaching a settled inner judgement — the verb spans 'to think/suppose' through 'to be certain.'
8.grammar: The connective 'wa' plus a past-tense verb. The '-ū' ending marks a masculine plural subject, 'they.' The doubled 'nn' belongs to the root.

9.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
9.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

10.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
10.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

12.meaning: A place of escape; a refuge or way out to flee to. A noun of place denoting any avenue of deliverance from danger — and often used in the negative, meaning 'no escape at all.'
12.grammar: A noun of place (the ma- prefix marking 'a place/means of'), with the weak middle root letter surfacing as long ī, meaning 'a place of escape.' The -in ending marks it indefinite ('any escape') and in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or in linkage with another noun. The doubled -in (tanwīn) signals indefiniteness.
12.root: ح-ي-ص (ḥ-y-ṣ) — to swerve aside, flee, escape, turn away from

1.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
1.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

2.meaning: Gets tired of / wearies of / despairs of — to become weary or lose enthusiasm for something through prolonged engagement; to tire of doing something.

parts.en: he (3rd person masculine singular imperfect prefix)
gets tired / grows weary (stem from the root 'to be weary')

2.grammar: Yasamu (more fully yasʾamu) is an imperfect (present/future) verb, 3rd person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks the imperfect singular masculine. The stem saʾm- comes from the root s-ʾ-m. The -u ending is the standard imperfect indicative vowel, marking an ordinary declarative statement ('he tires' / 'he does not tire'). The hamza between the sīn and the mīm may be reduced in recitation (hence the dagger mark in the written form).
2.root: س-أ-م (s-ʾ-m) — to be weary, to be bored, to tire of something

3.meaning: 'Mankind, the human being, humanity' — the human as a species or as the representative human creature.
3.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') here generalises to the whole class ('humankind as such'). The final -u is the nominative ending, the case that typically marks the subject (the doer or the thing spoken about) of a sentence.
3.root: ا-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humankind

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: A call, supplication, or invocation; the act of calling upon Allah in entreaty, prayer, or petition.
5.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action 'calling / supplicating'). The final -i is the genitive ending, the case that usually marks possession, links the word to a following noun ('… of …'), or follows a preposition. Here the genitive is produced by a construct (iḍāfa) link to a following possessor; the -i is purely the case vowel and does not itself encode any pronoun. When a first-person possessor ('my') is understood, that meaning comes from a possessive yāʾ that has been elided, not from the genitive vowel.

6.meaning: The good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a quality or as desirable things.
6.grammar: The definite article 'the' attached to the noun 'good/goodness', which carries the -i (genitive) ending. Here the genitive is governed by a preceding preposition meaning 'toward', so the phrase reads 'toward the good'. The word covers both moral goodness and beneficial things in general.
6.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, to choose what is best

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
7.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

8.meaning: it touched him, befell him, or afflicted him — said of harm or experience reaching and affecting a person.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning 'to touch, reach, or befall'. The third-person masculine singular subject ('he / it') is marked by a zero (null) suffix — there is no overt subject ending. The visible -a (fatḥa) on the final radical is the stem's own vowel pattern, not a person marker. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him', the one touched or afflicted.
8.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, come into contact, befall

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'evil, harm, ill, adversity.' It denotes what is bad or hurtful — misfortune and wrongdoing, the opposite of good (khayr).
9.grammar: The article al- makes it definite ('the'); its 'l' assimilates into the following 'sh' sound (so it is pronounced ash-sharr). The final -u is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject (the doer) of a sentence.
9.root: ش-ر-ر (sh-r-r) — to be evil, bad, harmful

10.meaning: one who loses hope; a person who gives up on any prospect of good coming to him — the word carries the sense of deep, settled despair rather than a momentary low mood

parts.en: one who despairs / a great despairer

10.grammar: The stem يَئُوس (yaūs) is a فَعُول (faʿūl) intensive adjective — it describes someone characteristically, habitually given to despair. The -un ending is the nominative indefinite marker (tanwīn ḍammah), indicating this is an indefinite noun or predicate in the nominative case. fa- is a light connective/consequential particle.
10.root: ي-أ-س (y-ʾ-s) — to despair, to lose hope

11.meaning: one who is deeply despondent; a person thoroughly given to hopelessness and despairing of mercy or good — similar in intensity to yaūs but with a slightly different nuance of visible, outward dejection

parts.en: one who despairs intensely / utterly hopeless

11.grammar: This is a فَعُول (faʿūl) intensive adjective pattern, denoting a person who characteristically exhibits the quality of qunūṭ (deep hopelessness). The -un ending is the nominative indefinite marker (tanwīn ḍammah), used when the word stands as a predicate or indefinite subject in the nominative case.
11.root: ق-ن-ط (q-n-ṭ) — to despair utterly, to be despondent

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

2.meaning: We made him taste — to give someone an experience of something, letting them feel or undergo it, as one tastes food. Used of letting a person experience either ease or hardship.

parts.en: made to taste, caused to experience (causative stem)

2.grammar: A past-tense causative verb (form IV) — the prefixed shape adds the sense 'to make/let [someone] do,' so the root 'to taste' becomes 'to make taste.' The -nā ending is the subject 'we' (completed past), and the attached -hu is the object 'him,' the one made to taste.
2.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste, to experience

3.meaning: Mercy: compassion that actively does good — tenderness joined with the will and power to relieve, forgive, and benefit. As a noun it names an instance or measure of such mercy.
3.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -an (accusative) ending, marked by tanwīn (the doubled-n sound). The accusative generally signals the word is a direct object or otherwise governed; the tanwīn marks it as indefinite — 'a mercy', 'some mercy'.

4.meaning: 'From us' — the preposition 'from' fused with the pronoun 'us,' indicating source or origin in the first-person plural.
4.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / out of') with the attached pronoun '-nā' ('us'). The nūn of 'min' assimilates into the following 'n', producing the doubled 'minnā.' It marks origin or source: 'from us / on our part.'

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
6.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
6.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

7.meaning: 'Adversity / harm / hardship / distress' — affliction or suffering that touches a person, the opposite of ease and well-being.
7.grammar: A feminine noun on an intensive pattern denoting a state of harm or distress. The final -a is the accusative case, the form typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing affected or undergone). This pattern does not take nunation, so there is no -n sound.
7.root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — to harm, injure, cause distress

8.meaning: It touched him / befell him — when something (often hardship or harm) makes contact with and reaches a person, affecting them.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -t ending (the feminine -at, here without its vowel) marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she/it did') — used when the doer is a grammatically feminine noun. The attached -hu is the object 'him,' the one touched.

9.meaning: An emphatic verbal statement meaning 'he will surely say / he is bound to say.' The base verb is the ordinary verb of speaking and saying, here charged with strong emphasis so that the saying is presented as certain to occur.
9.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), doubly emphasized: the prefixed 'la-' ('surely') and the heavy suffixed '-nna' (the energetic) together turn the plain 'he says' into a firm assertion of what he will certainly say.

10.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
10.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

11.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
11.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

12.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
12.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
12.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

13.meaning: I suppose, think, or reckon; to hold an opinion or surmise, often with a sense of supposition or conjecture rather than certain knowledge.
13.grammar: A present/future verb. The 'a-' prefix marks the first-person singular 'I'. The '-u' ending is the indicative mood, the default form used for an ongoing or plain statement ('I suppose').
13.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, think, conjecture

14.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hour' — most particularly the Last Hour, the appointed time of the world's end and the Resurrection; literally a portion of time, an hour, or a moment.
14.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- (its l assimilates into the following 'sun letter' s, hence the doubled s). The -a ending is the accusative case, the case typically taken by the direct object of a verb or by what follows certain particles.
14.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a span of time, an hour; the appointed Hour

15.meaning: Standing, established, or coming to pass; that which arises or occurs. As a feminine active participle it describes the one (feminine) who/which stands or comes about.
15.grammar: An active participle ('the one standing/occurring'), made feminine by the '-a(t)' ending. The final '-an' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a …') and in the accusative case, the form used for objects or predicates of certain verbs.

16.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
16.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

17.meaning: I was returned; I have been brought back — referring to being restored or returned to something, often used when a person contemplates being sent back (to a prior state, to life, or before Allah)

parts.en: I (first person singular past tense suffix)

17.grammar: This is the passive voice of the Form I verb رَجَعَ (rajaʿa). The pattern رُجِعَ (rujiʿa) is the passive past tense third-person form; here the suffix -tu shifts it to the first person singular: 'I was returned.' The u-vowel on the first radical and i-vowel on the second are the hallmarks of the Arabic passive past. The -tu ending is the standard first-person singular past-tense marker in both active and passive constructions.
17.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, to go back, to be restored

18.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
18.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

19.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
19.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
19.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

20.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
20.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

21.meaning: 'to Me' or 'for Me' — the preposition 'to/for' fused with the first-person pronoun, expressing direction, benefit, or belonging toward the speaker.
21.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') with the attached pronoun '-ī' ('me'). Together they express benefit, direction, or attribution toward the first person.

22.meaning: 'With him / in his keeping / that he has' — combining the locational word 'ind ('at, with, in the presence/possession of') with the pronoun 'him'. It conveys that something is held by, present with, or belongs to him.
22.grammar: 'ʿinda' is an adverb of place/possession that always governs a following word in the genitive; here it takes the attached pronoun -hu ('him/his'). The -a on 'ʿinda' is its fixed accusative-style ending as an adverbial. The pronoun -hu means the thing is located with, or owned by, a single male.

23.meaning: the best (thing / outcome / state); the finest, most excellent result — often refers to a good fate, a blessed recompense, or the most favorable condition Allah can grant
23.grammar: The la- is a lam al-tawkīd (emphatic lam, 'surely/indeed'). The definite article al- assimilates to the following ḥ. الحُسۡنٰى (al-ḥusnā) is the feminine superlative ('the best'), built on the فُعۡلَى (fuʿlā) pattern — the feminine counterpart of the masculine superlative أَفۡعَل. حُسۡنَى fits this pattern directly from the root ح-س-ن. The final ā (written as alif maqsūrah ـٰى) is the feminine superlative suffix; the word is indeclinable in this pattern (it does not take case vowels), so its grammatical role must be read from context rather than from its ending.

24.meaning: but We will surely inform them; We will certainly make known — an emphatic divine declaration of giving definitive information or news to someone

parts.en: inform / notify (Form II stem: to tell, to bring news)

24.grammar: The verb is Form II (فَعَّلَ) of the root, meaning 'to inform, to notify.' The construction la- + verb + emphatic nūn (nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīlah) is a very strong double emphasis: 'We will most certainly inform.' The prefix nu- marks first person plural (we). The emphatic nūn attached at the end is the heavy nūn of emphasis (نون التوكيد الثقيلة), used with oath and emphatic lam constructions to reinforce certainty; it causes the final vowel of the verb to be fatḥah before it.
24.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — to bring news, to inform, to notify

25.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
25.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

26.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
26.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

27.meaning: A compound meaning roughly 'because of what...', 'on account of that which...', or 'by means of what...'. It joins the preposition 'with/by/because of' to a connector 'what/that which', introducing the reason or instrument for something.
27.grammar: A preposition (bi-) fused to the word mā ('what / that which'). The preposition bi- expresses cause, means, or accompaniment; combined with mā it forms a phrase pointing to the thing or fact that serves as a reason or means ('because of what...').

28.meaning: They did / they worked — to perform a deed or action, to do work. The base word covers purposeful action and labor.
28.grammar: A completed-action (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending marks 'they' (a group of males) as the doers (the silent alif after it is a spelling convention).
28.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, act, work, perform a deed

29.meaning: A verb meaning 'and We will most certainly make them taste' — causing someone to experience or undergo something (often a punishment), stated with the strongest emphasis. 'Tasting' is used figuratively for being made to feel and undergo something.

parts.en: make taste / cause to experience (verb stem)

29.grammar: A present/future verb loaded with emphasis: prefixed 'wa-' ('and') and 'la-' ('surely'), with the doubled '-nna' ending (the 'heavy' emphatic) adding 'most certainly.' The 'nu-' prefix marks the doer as 'we'; the attached '-hum' is the object 'them.' This Form IV verb means to make someone taste or undergo something.
29.root: ذ-و-ق (dh-w-q) — to taste; (Form IV) to make experience

30.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
30.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

31.meaning: A punishment / torment — painful chastisement or suffering imposed as a penalty. The word names the punishment itself, stated indefinitely ('a punishment').
31.grammar: A noun, 'punishment/torment'. The final -in (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and genitive in case — the form used after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of a punishment').

32.meaning: An adjective meaning 'harsh, rough, severe, coarse' — thick or crude in texture, and by extension stern, grievous, or heavy when describing punishment or treatment.
32.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern. The final -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn), marking it indefinite; this ending typically appears when the word follows a preposition or modifies a genitive (often-translated '… of …') noun.
32.root: غ-ل-ظ (gh-l-ẓ) — to be thick, coarse, harsh, severe

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: 'We bestowed favor / granted blessing / showed grace.' The verb conveys conferring comfort, ease, and good things upon someone — to favor and provide bounty.

parts.en: bestow favor / grant blessing (causative verb stem)

2.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in the causative pattern (af'ala), 'to confer favor.' The attached -nā is the first-person plural subject ('we'), marking the doers of a finished action. The action is presented as accomplished.
2.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — favor, blessing, ease, bounty

3.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
3.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
3.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

4.meaning: The human being; mankind or a person, the species of humans as distinct from other creatures.
4.grammar: A definite noun: al- is 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when it is possessed by a preceding noun (the '… of …' relationship).
4.root: أ-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — to be sociable, familiar; humankind

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'he turned away' or 'he averted himself' — deliberately turning aside from something, shunning or disregarding it.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The final '-a' marks the doer as 'he' (third-person masculine singular). This Form IV verb conveys deliberately turning one's side away from something — to shun, avoid, or disregard it.
5.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — side; (Form IV) to turn away from

6.meaning: 'And he kept his distance / turned away / withdrew.' The verb conveys becoming far or remote — drawing back and putting space between oneself and another.

parts.en: he became distant / drew away (past-tense verb)

6.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The core is a completed (past-tense) hollow verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he'), describing a finished action of becoming distant or withdrawing.
6.root: ن-أ-ي (n-ʾ-y) — to be far, distant, withdraw, keep aloof

7.meaning: 'With/by his side.' It joins the preposition 'with/by' to the noun 'side' (a person's flank or self) plus 'his,' yielding the sense of turning aside or holding oneself apart — literally 'with his side (turned away).'
7.grammar: The prefix bi- is the preposition 'with/by.' A noun governed by a preposition takes the genitive, shown here by the -i vowel before the pronoun. The attached -hi means 'his.' Together the phrase functions adverbially, describing manner ('turning his side away').
7.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side, flank, to be beside or to turn aside

8.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
8.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

9.meaning: 'It touched him / afflicted him / befell him.' The verb conveys contact reaching a person — something making contact with or coming upon someone, often used of an affliction striking.
9.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he/it'), with the doubled root letter characteristic of this verb. The attached -hu is the direct object 'him.' It states that the touching has occurred.
9.root: م-س-س (m-s-s) — to touch, make contact, afflict

10.meaning: A noun meaning 'evil, harm, ill, adversity.' It denotes what is bad or hurtful — misfortune and wrongdoing, the opposite of good (khayr).
10.grammar: The article al- makes it definite ('the'); its 'l' assimilates into the following 'sh' sound (so it is pronounced ash-sharr). The final -u is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject (the doer) of a sentence.
10.root: ش-ر-ر (sh-r-r) — to be evil, bad, harmful

11.meaning: then (he is) possessed of; one who has / is endowed with — used to indicate that someone possesses a quality or attribute; it is a noun of possession that must always be followed by a noun describing what is possessed
11.grammar: ذُو (dhū) belongs to the class of أسماء الخمسة (the five nouns), which change their vowel to show case: dhū (nominative, owner/possessor of), dhī (genitive), dhā (accusative). The -ū ending here is the nominative case marker for this special noun class, indicating the word stands as a subject or predicate in the nominative. fa- is a connective consequential particle.
11.root: ذ-و-ي (dh-w-y) — to possess, to own (defective root used for ذو)

12.meaning: supplication; calling out to Allah; earnest prayer — the act of invoking or calling upon Allah, whether in need, petition, praise, or in general worship through words
12.grammar: دُعَاء (duʿāʾ) is a verbal noun (مصدر) from the Form I verb دَعَا (daʿā — to call, to supplicate). The ending -in is the genitive indefinite marker (tanwīn kasr), which appears because the word follows a possessive construction or a governing word that places it in the genitive case. The genitive typically marks the second noun in a possessive chain (iḍāfah), or follows a preposition.
12.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invoke, to supplicate

13.meaning: wide; broad; extensive; lengthy — describes something that is spacious or far-reaching in scope; when applied to supplication it conveys the sense of a prayer that is long, wide-ranging, and persistent
13.grammar: عَرِيض (ʿarīḍ) is a فَعِيل (faʿīl) adjective pattern, commonly used for stable, inherent qualities. The ending -in is the genitive indefinite marker (tanwīn kasr), showing the adjective agrees in case, gender, and definiteness with the noun it modifies, which is in the genitive indefinite. Adjectives in Arabic follow and agree with their nouns in all four categories.
13.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — width, breadth, to be wide

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A rhetorical address meaning roughly 'Have you considered?' or 'Tell me — what do you think of…?'. It combines the question particle 'a-' ('do/have…?') with the verb 'to see', here in the sense of mentally considering or reflecting on something rather than literal eyesight. It is addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: A past-tense verb carrying a subject built into its ending: the '-tum' ending marks a completed action done by 'you all' (masculine plural). Prefixed with the question particle 'a-', it turns the statement into a question, idiomatically 'have you considered / tell me'.
2.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — seeing, perceiving, considering

3.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
3.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

4.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

4.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

6.meaning: 'In the presence of / from with / from the side of' — a noun of place and source meaning nearness or 'with,' used for what is in someone's keeping, possession, or vicinity, and figuratively what proceeds from them.
6.grammar: An adverbial noun meaning 'at / with / in the presence of,' here in the genitive case (the -i ending), as happens when it follows a preposition or links to a following noun ('the presence OF …'). It typically expresses 'from the side of' or 'in the keeping of' someone.
6.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, near, or with; presence and proximity

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
8.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

9.meaning: To disbelieve, reject faith, or be ungrateful — to cover over and deny the truth, refusing to acknowledge Allah or His favor. The root sense is 'to cover/conceal,' so disbelief is pictured as veiling what one knows to be true. With the ending it means 'you (all) disbelieved.'

parts.en: you all (masculine plural) — past-tense subject ending

9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action. The suffix -tum marks the doer as second-person masculine plural ('you all'), so the whole word means 'you all disbelieved.'
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to deny/reject (disbelief, ingratitude)

10.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
10.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

11.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
11.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
11.root: — (pronoun)

12.meaning: More astray / further off the path — the comparative form: even more lost or further from the right way than something else.
12.grammar: A comparative adjective: 'more astray.' The af'al pattern conveys 'more/most ___.' The -u ending is the nominative case, typically marking the word as a subject or predicate (the thing being described).
12.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, err

13.meaning: A compound meaning 'than one who / than whoever' — combining the preposition of comparison 'than' with the relative pronoun 'who', used to compare a person against others.
13.grammar: The preposition 'min' (here 'than', used after elatives) followed by the indeclinable relative 'man' ('who'). The final nūn of 'min' undergoes regressive assimilation into the following mīm of 'man', producing a doubled mīm; the resulting shadda sits on the mīm of 'man'. Both words are indeclinable particles and take no case ending.

14.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
14.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

15.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
15.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

16.meaning: 'Schism, split, discord, opposition' — a state of being in conflict or at odds, two sides set against each other.
16.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The ending '-in' combines genitive case with indefiniteness ('a …'), the doubled 'n' sound (tanwīn) marking it as indefinite; this case typically follows a preposition or links the noun to a preceding noun.
16.root: ش-ق-ق (sh-q-q) — to split, cleave; division, discord

17.meaning: Far, distant, remote — describing something separated by a great distance in space, time, or relation.
17.grammar: An adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which typically conveys a settled or intensive quality ('far-off'). The final -in (tanwīn kasra) marks it as indefinite ('a far thing') and in the genitive case — the case a noun or adjective takes after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive (iḍāfa) construction.

1.meaning: We will soon show them; We are going to make them see — a divine promise or declaration that Allah will cause certain people to witness or perceive something

parts.en: show / make see (Form IV stem of to see/show)
them (third person masculine plural object pronoun)

1.grammar: The verb is Form IV (أفعل) of the root ر-أ-ي, meaning 'to show, to make someone see.' The prefix sa- signals the near future ('will/soon'). The prefix nu- marks the first person plural subject ('we'). The attached pronoun -him is the third person masculine plural object ('them'). Together sa-nu-rī-him means 'We will soon show them.' The stem rī here is the contracted imperfect Form IV stem (أَرَى → نُرِي).
1.root: ر-أ-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see; Form IV: to show, to make see

2.meaning: Our signs / verses. The plural of āya — a sign, token, or miraculous proof, and also a verse of revelation — with the attached 'our'.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun ('signs / verses') with the possessive pronoun -nā ('our'). The sound feminine plural ending -āt shows -i, the case used for the genitive (linked to a following word or after a preposition) and the accusative (object of a verb); attaching -nā ('our') also places it in a possessive relationship. So it means 'signs belonging to Us'.
2.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — sign, mark, token

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: the horizons; the far reaches of the sky and earth; the distant edges of the universe in all directions — used to refer to the outer regions of the cosmos that lie beyond one's immediate view
4.grammar: آفَاق (āfāq) is the broken plural of أُفُق (ufuq, 'horizon'), following the أَفۡعَال (ʾafʿāl) pattern — a triliteral broken plural pattern common for nouns of this structure. The -i ending (kasr) is the genitive case marker, indicating the word follows a preposition or forms part of a possessive construction. The definite article al- (assimilated to the following vowel) makes it 'the horizons' rather than indefinite.
4.root: أ-ف-ق (ʾ-f-q) — horizon, the far reaches of sky and earth

5.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
5.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

6.meaning: Themselves / their own selves — the noun nafs ('self, soul, person, inner being') joined to a pronoun 'their'. Used reflexively it means 'their own selves' and conveys the inmost self, the seat of desires and the person as a whole.
6.grammar: The plural noun anfus ('selves') carries the genitive -i ending followed by the possessive pronoun -him ('their'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -him makes it 'their selves'.
6.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

7.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
7.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

8.meaning: 'It becomes clear / distinct.' For something to become evident and clearly set apart, so that it is plainly distinguished and no longer confused with anything else.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb (form V, 'to become clear/distinct'), third-person masculine singular ('it becomes clear'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he/it' subject. The final -a is the subjunctive (manṣūb) ending: the verb is governed by a preceding particle (such as ḥattā, 'until/so that') that subordinates it, which is why it ends in -a rather than the indicative -u. Form V typically describes a gradual process or a state coming about of itself — here, something emerging into clarity.
8.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — to be clear, distinct, evident; separation

9.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

10.meaning: 'That it (is) …' The emphasizing particle 'anna' ('that … indeed') with an attached 'it/he,' used to introduce a firmly asserted statement and tie it to a preceding verb such as 'know' or 'say.'
10.grammar: The particle anna ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -hu ('it/he,' masculine singular) as its subject. Anna introduces a strongly affirmed noun-clause ('that it is indeed…') and places its subject in the accusative; it commonly follows verbs of knowing, saying, or believing.
10.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

11.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
11.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
11.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

12.meaning: A compound opening a question and a negation at once: roughly 'and have … not …?' or 'is it not the case that …?'. It combines a questioning particle, the connector 'and', and a negative that places the following verb in the past, often expecting the listener to agree.
12.grammar: Three particles fused together: the interrogative 'a-' (turning the statement into a question), the connector 'wa' ('and'), and the negator 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and shifts its meaning into the past ('has not / did not'), and it puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (vowel-less) form. The combination often invites the listener to affirm ('have you not …?').
12.root: — (particles)

13.meaning: is sufficient; is enough — indicates that something is adequate or meets the need entirely, often used to assert that Allah alone is sufficient for a given purpose

parts.en: is sufficient / suffices (third person masculine singular imperfect, jussive)

13.grammar: يَكۡفِ is the imperfect (present/future) tense of the Form I verb كَفَى (kafā — to be sufficient, to suffice). The prefix ya- marks the third person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -i (kasrah) on the apocopated form represents the jussive mood (مجزوم); in the jussive the final weak letter (the ي of كفى) is dropped and a sukūn or a short vowel remains. The jussive appears here after a conditional or negative particle that governs it. The word conveys that something fully meets a need with nothing lacking.
13.root: ك-ف-ي (k-f-y) — to suffice, to be enough, to spare someone from need

14.meaning: By/with your Lord. 'Rabb' is the Lord who creates, owns, sustains, and nurtures His creation to its completion — a Master who provides for and governs all that He has made.
14.grammar: The preposition 'bi-' ('by/with') attached to the noun 'rabb,' which takes the genitive '-i' ending because a noun after a preposition is put in the genitive case; '-ka' is the possessive 'your.'
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master; lordship

15.meaning: 'That it (is) …' The emphasizing particle 'anna' ('that … indeed') with an attached 'it/he,' used to introduce a firmly asserted statement and tie it to a preceding verb such as 'know' or 'say.'
15.grammar: The particle anna ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun -hu ('it/he,' masculine singular) as its subject. Anna introduces a strongly affirmed noun-clause ('that it is indeed…') and places its subject in the accusative; it commonly follows verbs of knowing, saying, or believing.

16.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
16.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

17.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
17.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

18.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
18.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
18.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

19.meaning: A witness — one who sees and observes directly and can testify to what is true; also carries the sense of an ever-watchful observer.
19.grammar: An intensive descriptive noun (pattern 'faʿīl') meaning one who witnesses fully and constantly. The '-un' ending is nominative and indefinite: the nominative typically marks the subject or predicate ('is a witness'), and the final 'n' sound marks it indefinite.

1.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
1.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

2.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
2.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: Doubt, uncertainty, or wavering suspicion — a state of being unsure or in dispute about something.
4.grammar: A feminine noun. The '-in' ending combines the genitive case (the case after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage) with indefiniteness ('some doubt / any doubt'); the final '-n' sound is nunation, the mark of an indefinite noun.
4.root: م-ر-ي (m-r-y) — to doubt, dispute, be uncertain

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: meeting; encounter; coming face to face — in Qur'anic usage it most often refers to the meeting with Allah on the Day of Judgment, the inevitable encounter every soul will have before its Lord
6.grammar: لِقَاء (liqāʾ) is a verbal noun (مصدر) of the Form I verb لَقِيَ (laqiya — to meet, to encounter). The ending -i (kasrah) is the genitive case marker, indicating the word follows a preposition or is the second noun in a possessive chain (iḍāfah). When preceded by a preposition such as بِ (bi-) it reads 'of/with the meeting' or 'to the meeting,' linking it to what it modifies.
6.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, to encounter, to come face to face

7.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
7.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

8.meaning: An opening particle of alert and emphasis — 'Now then!', 'Beware!', 'Truly!'. It calls attention to and strongly affirms the statement that follows.
8.grammar: An attention-drawing particle placed at the start of a statement. It rouses the listener and emphasizes what comes next, somewhat like 'Indeed!', 'Lo!', or 'Take note!' in English.

9.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
9.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

10.meaning: 'Of every / with all' — the preposition 'bi' ('with / in / by') joined to the word 'every / each / all', expressing comprehensiveness applied to whatever noun follows.
10.grammar: A preposition plus a noun. The prefix bi- ('with / in / by') always places the following noun in the genitive ('of') state. The final -i on 'kull' is that genitive ending, signalling the word is governed by the preposition. 'Kull' denotes totality — 'every (single)' or 'all'.
10.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, completeness, all-ness

11.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
11.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
11.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

12.meaning: all-encompassing; surrounding on every side; one who surrounds and encompasses everything — an attribute conveying absolute, total encirclement with no gap or escape; nothing lies outside the reach of what is described
12.grammar: مُحِيط (muḥīṭ) is the active participle (اسم الفاعل) of the Form IV verb أَحَاطَ (aḥāṭa — to surround, to encompass). The Form IV active participle follows the pattern مُفْعِل (mufʿil). The -un ending is the nominative indefinite marker (tanwīn ḍammah), indicating the word is in the nominative case, typically as a predicate ('is all-encompassing') or as an indefinite subject. As a divine attribute it communicates that Allah's knowledge, power, and presence surround all things completely.
12.root: ح-و-ط (ḥ-w-ṭ) — to surround, to encircle, to encompass
